questions.question: Let C be a circle with centre O. Let AB be a tangent to C such that AB touches the circle at point P. Let X and Y be any two points on C. If ∠APX = 50° and ∠BPY = 60°, then find ∠PXY and ∠PYX, respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the Alternate Segment Theorem: Angle between tangent and chord = Angle in the alternate segment.

For chord PX and tangent AP: ∠PYX = ∠APX = 50°.

For chord PY and tangent BP: ∠PXY = ∠BPY = 60°.

Required values: ∠PXY = 60° and ∠PYX = 50°.

**∴ Answer = 60°, 50°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Tangent AB touches circle C at point P. Points X and Y are on the circle. ∠APX = 50° and ∠BPY = 60°.

**Formula used:**

Alternate Segment Theorem: The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

 
• A B P 
• 
• 
• X Y 50° 60° 60° 50° Tangent AB at P 

**Calculations:**

According to the Alternate Segment Theorem:

⇒ Angle between tangent BP and chord PY = Angle subtended by chord PY at point X

⇒ ∠BPY = ∠PXY

⇒ ∠PXY = 60°

⇒ Angle between tangent AP and chord PX = Angle subtended by chord PX at point Y

⇒ ∠APX = ∠PYX

⇒ ∠PYX = 50°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°, 50°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Segment Theorem

For any chord of a circle, the angle it makes with a tangent through one of its endpoints is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

Tangent-Radius Property

A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact (Angle between radius and tangent = 90°).

Angle in Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of a circle is always 90°.

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc (or chord) at any points on the remaining part of the circle are equal.

questions.question: Which of the following social reformers established the ‘Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha’ in 1924?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**B R Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha** was a central institution formed by **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar** for removing the difficulties of the **untouchables** and placing their grievances before the government.
 
• It was established on **20 July 1924** at **Bombay** (now **Mumbai**), **Maharashtra**.
 
• The main **objective** of the **Sabha** was to promote the **spread of education** among the **depressed classes** by opening hostels, libraries, and social centers.
 
• The institution focused on the **socio-economic improvement** of the **Dalit** community, aiming to instill a sense of **self-respect** and **dignity**. ***Hence, the association of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar with this Sabha is correct.***
 
• The famous **motto** of this organization was **"Educate, Agitate, Organize,"** which became a rallying cry for the **anti-caste movement** in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jyotirao Phule:**

 
 
• He was a prominent **social reformer** from **Maharashtra** who founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** (Truth Seekers' Society) on **24 September 1873**.
 
• He worked extensively for the **education of women** and lower-caste people, opening the first school for girls in **Pune** in **1848**.
 
• He was bestowed with the title of **Mahatma** in **1888** for his selfless service to society.
 
 
 
• **Baba Amte:**
 
 
• **Muralidhar Devidas Amte**, popularly known as **Baba Amte**, was a **social activist** known for his work in the **rehabilitation and empowerment** of people suffering from **leprosy**.
 
• He founded the **Anandwan** (Forest of Bliss) ashram in **1949** in **Chandrapur** district, **Maharashtra**.
 
• He was awarded the **Ramon Magsaysay Award** in **1985** and the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1986**.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:**
 
 
• He was the **first Prime Minister** of independent **India** and a central figure in **Indian politics** before and after independence.
 
• He served as the **President** of the **Indian National Congress** multiple times, notably during the **Lahore Session** in **1929** where **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence) was declared.
 
• He is the author of famous books like **"The Discovery of India"** and **"Glimpses of World History."**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar** served as the **Chairman** of the **Drafting Committee** of the **Constitution of India** and is widely regarded as the **Father of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• He led the **Mahad Satyagraha** in **1927** to assert the rights of **untouchables** to use water from public tanks.
 
• In **1932**, he signed the **Poona Pact** with **Mahatma Gandhi**, which secured **reserved seats** for the **Depressed Classes** in the provisional legislatures.
 
• He founded the **Independent Labour Party** in **1936** and the **Scheduled Castes Federation** in **1942**.
 
• In his later years, specifically on **14 October 1956**, he converted to **Buddhism** along with lakhs of his followers in **Nagpur**.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian honor, in the year **1990**.

If ‘+’ means ‘−’, ‘−’ means ‘×’, ‘×’ means ‘÷’, ‘÷’ means ‘+’, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

57 − 7 ÷ 119 + 288 × 2 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7751840ca1840d12cadc428f84d30e2cdcd5e7f82d52a57de21f2404c58eed88.png] 

Given equation: **57 − 7 ÷ 119 + 288 × 2 = ?**

Now, if + means ‘−’, − means ‘×’, × means ‘÷’, ÷ means ‘+’, then:

⇒ 57 × 7 + 119 − 288 ÷ 2

⇒ 57 × 7 = 399

⇒ 288 ÷ 2 = 144

⇒ 399 + 119 − 144

⇒ 518 − 144

⇒ 374

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

questions.question: Which provision in Part II of the Constitution defines one basis for citizenship at the commencement, specifically that the person’s either parent was born in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 5**__.

• **Article 5** of the **Indian Constitution** provides for citizenship at the **commencement of the Constitution**, which took place on **January 26, 1950**.
 
• According to this Article, every person who had their **domicile** in the territory of India at that time and fulfilled one of the three conditions became a **citizen of India**.
 
• The specific condition mentioned in the question is found in **Article 5(b)**, which states that a person becomes a citizen if **either of whose parents was born in the territory of India**. ***Hence, the statement regarding parentage as a basis for citizenship is correct under Article 5.***
 
• The other two conditions under **Article 5** include being **born in the territory of India** (Article 5a) or being **ordinarily resident** in India for **not less than five years** immediately preceding the commencement (Article 5c).

questions.question: What is the maximum value that must be assigned to A so that the 8-digit number 588A9792 is divisible by 4?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisibility rule for 4: Only the last two digits of the number must be divisible by 4.

Last two digits of 588A9792 are 92.

92 ÷ 4 = 23 (Remainder = 0).

Since 92 is divisible by 4, the digit A can be any value from 0 to 9.

The maximum single-digit value for A is 9.

**∴ Answer = 9** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Number = 588A9792

Condition: The number must be divisible by 4.

**Formula used:**

Divisibility by 4: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 4.

 Checking Divisibility of 588A9792 by 4 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 5 8 8 A 9 7 9 2 Any Digit (0-9) Last 2 digits: 92 92 ÷ 4 = 23 (OK) 

**Calculations:**

Identify the last two digits of the number 588A9792, which are 92.

⇒ Check divisibility of 92 by 4: 92 ÷ 4 = 23.

⇒ Since 92 is divisible by 4, the value of the digit A does not affect the divisibility of the entire number by 4.

⇒ The digit A can take any integer value from 0 to 9 inclusive.

⇒ To find the maximum value of A, we pick the largest single-digit integer.

⇒ Maximum value of A = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the last three digits of the number are divisible by 8. For 588A9792, 792 ÷ 8 = 99, so it is also divisible by 8.

Divisibility by 2

A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even (0, 2, 4, 6, or 8).

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. Sum = 5+8+8+A+9+7+9+2 = 48 + A.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and even positions is 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: Which folk music form of Uttar Pradesh is traditionally sung during the monsoon season by women?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kajri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kajri** is one of the most popular folk music forms of **Uttar Pradesh** and **Bihar**, specifically associated with the **monsoon season** (the month of **Sawan**). It is traditionally sung by **women** as they express their feelings of longing for their husbands or lovers while swinging on trees during the rains. *Hence, the option Kajri is the correct answer.*
 
• The origin of **Kajri** is believed to be in the **Mirzapur** district of **Uttar Pradesh**. According to local folklore, it is named after **Kajli**, a woman who sang songs of separation while waiting for her husband.
 
• It is often performed in two styles: **Dhunmuniya Kajri**, which is sung in a circle without any musical instruments, and **Baithaki Kajri**, which is a more formal rendition performed in a seated gathering with instruments like the **Harmonium** and **Tabla**.
 
• The themes of **Kajri** usually revolve around the beauty of the **rainy season**, the dark clouds, the greenery, and the divine love stories of **Radha** and **Lord Krishna**.
 
• The language used in these songs is predominantly **Bhojpuri**, **Maithili**, or **Awadhi**, reflecting the local culture of the **Purvanchal** region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lavani**:

 
 
• This is a traditional folk song and dance form from the state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• It is characterized by a powerful rhythm provided by the **Dholki** and is usually performed by **women** wearing **nine-yard long saris** (Nauvari).
 
• It covers various topics like **politics**, **religion**, and **romance**, and was traditionally used to entertain soldiers during the **18th** and **19th centuries**.
 
 
 
• **Bhatiali**:
 
 
• This is a form of folk music from **West Bengal** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• It is traditionally sung by **boatmen** (malla) while rowing down the rivers of the **Ganges** delta.
 
• The word is derived from '**Bhata**', meaning **ebb** or downstream, as these songs are sung while going with the flow of the river.
 
 
 
• **Maand (Maang)**:
 
 
• This is a sophisticated style of folk singing from **Rajasthan**.
 
• It is neither purely classical nor purely folk but sits somewhere in between. It is famous for the song '**Kesariya Balam**', which welcomes guests to the state.
 
• It was traditionally patronized by the **Rajput** royalty and developed in the **Bikaner** and **Jaisalmer** regions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Semi-Classical Integration**: **Kajri** has been adopted into **Indian Classical Music**, particularly by the **Banaras Gharana**. Legendary singers like **Girija Devi**, known as the '**Queen of Thumri**', were instrumental in popularizing **Kajri** on global stages.
 
• **Geographical Identity**: While it is the state folk song of **Uttar Pradesh**, it is also celebrated during the **Kajli Teej** festival in **Varanasi** and **Mirzapur**, where large-scale competitions are held.
 
• **Cultural Impact**: Other notable folk forms of **Uttar Pradesh** include **Rasiya** (Braj region), **Chaiti** (sung in the month of Chaitra), and **Birha** (narrative ballads usually sung by the **Ahir** community).
 
• **Linguistic Diversity**: The **Kajri** songs often use **Braj Bhasha** and **Bhojpuri** dialects, making them an essential part of the **Indo-Gangetic** cultural heritage.

questions.question: Which battle is regarded as the turning point that led to British political control in Bengal and opened the path for British expansion in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Battle of Plassey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Plassey** took place on **23 June 1757** and is widely regarded as the decisive turning point that initiated **British political control** in **India**. ***Hence, the option Battle of Plassey is correct.***
 
• The conflict was fought at **Palashi** (Plassey), located on the banks of the **Bhagirathi River** in **Bengal**, between the forces of the **British East India Company** and the **Nawab of Bengal**, **Siraj-ud-Daulah**.
 
• The **British** forces were led by **Robert Clive**, who utilized the internal conspiracies within the Nawab’s court to his advantage, specifically the betrayal of **Mir Jafar**, the commander-in-chief of the Nawab's army.
 
• As a result of this victory, the **British East India Company** gained significant influence over the administration of **Bengal**, which was the richest province of **India** at the time. This provided the **British** with the financial resources necessary for further **military expansion** across the subcontinent.
 
• This battle marked the transition of the **East India Company** from a mere **trading entity** to a **political power**, setting the stage for nearly two centuries of **British colonial rule**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Battle of Buxar (1764):**

 
 
• Fought on **22nd October 1764**, this battle was between the **British East India Company**, led by **Hector Munro**, and a combined alliance of **Mir Qasim** (the Nawab of Bengal), **Shuja-ud-Daulah** (the Nawab of Awadh), and **Shah Alam II** (the Mughal Emperor).
 
• Unlike Plassey, this was a hard-fought military victory that firmly established **British sovereignty** over **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Odisha**.
 
• It culminated in the **Treaty of Allahabad** in **1765**, which granted **Diwani Rights** (the right to collect revenues) to the **British**. ***Hence, the option Battle of Buxar is incorrect as the primary turning point.***
 
 
 
• **Battle of Wandiwash (1760):**
 
 
• This was a crucial battle in **South India** fought on **22 January 1760** during the **Third Carnatic War**.
 
• It took place between the **French** (under **Comte de Lally**) and the **British** (under **Sir Eyre Coote**) at **Wandiwash** (Tamil Nadu).
 
• The decisive **British victory** effectively ended **French** imperial ambitions in **India**, limiting them to small enclaves like **Puducherry**. ***Hence, the option Battle of Wandiwash is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Third Carnatic War (1758–1763):**
 
 
• This was the local manifestation of the global **Seven Years' War** between **Britain** and **France**.
 
• The conflict concluded with the **Treaty of Paris** in **1763**, which restored **French** factories in **India** but prohibited them from fortifying their settlements, ensuring **British supremacy** among European powers in **India**. ***Hence, the option Third Carnatic War is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Robert Clive:** Often called the "Conqueror of India," his leadership during the **Battle of Plassey** earned him the title of **Governor of Bengal**. He introduced the **Dual System of Government** (1765–1772) in **Bengal**.
 
• **Siraj-ud-Daulah:** The last independent **Nawab of Bengal**. His execution after the **Battle of Plassey** signaled the end of independent regional sovereignty in the **Bengal** region.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The control over **Bengal** allowed the **British** to stop the flow of **gold and silver** from **London** to **India** to buy goods; instead, they used the local revenues to purchase Indian textiles for export, leading to the **drain of wealth**.
 
• **Geopolitical Shift:** The **British** victory at **Plassey** and subsequently **Buxar** shifted the center of political gravity from the **Mughal** capital in **Delhi** to **Calcutta** (Kolkata).

questions.question: According to GFRA 2025, what was India’s global rank in total forest area?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 9__**th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Global Forest Resources Assessment (GFRA) 2025, released by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), India ranks 9th globally in total forest area.
 
• This marks an improvement from the previous 2020 assessment, where India was ranked 10th.
 
• Total Forest Area: India holds approximately 72.7 million hectares of forest, accounting for roughly 2% of the world's total forest cover.
 
• Annual Forest Gain: India continues to maintain the 3rd position worldwide for net annual forest area gain.
 
• Carbon Sinks: The country ranks 5th globally among top carbon sink nations, with its forests removing roughly 150 million tonnes of 

 per year.
 
• Bamboo Resources: India accounts for 11.8 million hectares of bamboo forests, which is nearly 40% of the global bamboo area.
 
• Top 5 Global Leaders: Over half of the world's forests are located in just five countries: Russia, Brazil, Canada, the USA, and China.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Forest Distribution:**

 
 
• The world’s total forest area is estimated at **4.1 billion hectares**, which is approximately **31%** of the total land area.
 
• More than half (**54%**) of the world’s forests are located in only five countries: the **Russian Federation**, **Brazil**, **Canada**, the **United States of America**, and **China**.
 
• **Russia** holds the largest share of the world's forests at **20%**, followed by **Brazil** at **12%**.
 
 
 
• **Rankings in Forest Gain:**
 
 
• In previous assessments like **GFRA 2020**, **India** was ranked **3rd** globally for the **average annual net gain** in forest area between **2010 and 2020**.
 
• This highlights that while **India** ranks **12th** in total size, its **growth rate** in forest cover has been among the highest in the world due to government initiatives.
 
 
 
• **FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization):**
 
 
• The **FAO** is a specialized agency of the **United Nations** that leads international efforts to defeat hunger and improve nutrition and food security.
 
• It was founded in **October 1945** and is headquartered in **Rome, Italy**.
 
• The **GFRA** report is published by the **FAO** every **five years** to help monitor sustainable forest management.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India State of Forest Report (ISFR):**

 
 
• In addition to international reports, **India** publishes its own **ISFR** biennially through the **Forest Survey of India (FSI)**, an organization under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**.
 
• The latest **ISFR** data aligns with global findings, showing a consistent increase in **tree cover** and **mangrove cover** across the country.
 
 
 
• **National Forest Policy:**
 
 
• The **National Forest Policy of 1988** set a target for **India** to have **33%** of its total geographical area under forest and tree cover to maintain **ecological balance**.
 
• Currently, **India's** forest and tree cover stands at approximately **24.62%** of its total geographical area, as per the last domestic survey.
 
 
 
• **Key Drivers:**
 
 
• Schemes like the **National Mission for a Green India (GIM)** and the **Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA)** are the primary drivers for increasing forest area in **India**.
 
• The **state of Madhya Pradesh** has the largest forest cover in **India** by area, while **Mizoram** has the highest forest cover as a percentage of total geographical area.

questions.question: A solid is composed of a cube surmounted by a cuboid. The edge of the cube is x cm. The cuboid placed on top has a square base exactly fitting the top face of the cube, and its height is (x − 4) cm. questions.question: Amir Khusrau, the famous historian, said about a particular language that *'*common people do not know it, only the Brahmanas do'*.* Which of the following languages did the historian talk about?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskrit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amir Khusrau**, the prolific **13th-14th century** poet and chronicler, made detailed observations about the linguistic diversity of **India** in his work titled **Nuh Sipihr** (The Nine Skies), written in **1318**.
 
• In this text, he listed several languages spoken across the subcontinent, such as **Sindhi**, **Lahori**, **Kashmiri**, **Dughri** (in Jammu), **Ma’bari** (in Tamil Nadu), **Gauri** (in Bengal), and **Gujari** (in Gujarat).
 
• He contrasted these regional languages with **Sanskrit**, noting that unlike others, it did not belong to any specific **geographic region**.
 
• **Amir Khusrau** remarked that **Sanskrit** was an **ancient language** that the **common people** did not know; its knowledge and use were restricted exclusively to the **Brahmanas**.

questions.question: If 6 machines can manufacture 480 components in 8 hours, how many components can 10 machines manufacture in 12 hours, assuming all machines work at the same constant rate?
questions.solution:

Work is directly proportional to the product of Machines and Time.

Initial Product = 6 machines × 8 hours = 48 machine-hours

Final Product = 10 machines × 12 hours = 120 machine-hours

Components = 480 × (120 ÷ 48) = 480 × 2.5 = 1200

(M₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂

⇒ 48 ÷ 480 = 120 ÷ W₂

⇒ 1 ÷ 10 = 120 ÷ W₂

__
 
• **Extensive farming** is characterized by a **low input** of labor, fertilizers, and capital relative to the **land area** being farmed. This system results in a **lower yield per unit of land** but covers vast geographical areas.
 
• **Intensive farming**, on the other hand, involves **high labor and capital inputs** aimed at maximizing the **production per land unit**. It uses a smaller amount of land to produce a **higher output** through the heavy use of fertilizers, pesticides, and technology.
 
• The **machinery type** used in both systems can vary, but it is not the defining difference; extensive farming often uses **large-scale machinery** for vast fields, while intensive farming uses **specialized equipment** for high-yield cycles. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Production per land unit** is the fundamental differentiator as it measures the efficiency and **intensity** of the agricultural output relative to the **hectares** cultivated. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• **Irrigation** can be used in both systems depending on the **climatic conditions** and **crop requirements**, so it does not serve as the primary distinguishing factor. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **size of seed** has no correlation with whether a farming system is extensive or intensive, as seed choice depends on the **crop variety** and **genetic traits**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Extensive Farming Characteristics:**

 
 
• This system is usually practiced in regions with **low population density** and abundant land availability, such as the **wheat belts** of the **USA**, **Canada**, **Australia**, and the **steppes of Russia**.
 
• The **total production** might be high due to the massive size of the farms, but the **output per hectare** remains relatively low compared to intensive methods.
 
• It involves **minimal use of chemical fertilizers** and relies more on the **natural fertility** of the soil.
 
 
 
• **Intensive Farming Characteristics:**
 
 
• Commonly practiced in **densely populated** countries like **India**, **China**, and **Japan**, where land is a scarce resource.
 
• It focuses on **Intensive Subsistence Agriculture** or **Commercial Intensive Farming** to meet the high demand for food.
 
• This method frequently employs **Multiple Cropping**, where more than one crop is grown on the same piece of land within a **single year**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• **Intensive farming** requires a much higher **initial investment** and **recurring expenditure** on **High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds**, **irrigation infrastructure**, and **energy**.
 
• **Extensive farming** is often more **environmentally sustainable** in terms of chemical runoff but requires significantly more **land transformation**.

• **Yield Comparison:** In **Intensive farming**, the yield per **unit area** is very high, but the **yield per person (labor)** might be low. In **Extensive farming**, the yield per **unit area** is low, but the **yield per labor unit** is very high due to **mechanization**.
 
• **Livestock Integration:** Extensive systems often include **pastoralism** and **ranching** where animals graze over large areas. Intensive systems include **factory farming** or **feedlots** where animals are kept in **confined spaces** with high-calorie feed.
 
• **Green Revolution:** The **1960s Green Revolution** in **India** shifted many regions from extensive or traditional subsistence methods toward **Intensive Commercial Farming** by introducing **chemical fertilizers** and **assured irrigation**.

Consider the following statements regarding the 74th Amendment Act of 1992.

1. It has added a new Part IX-A to the Constitution of India.

2. The Act has also added a new 10th Schedule to the Constitution.

3. The Act provides for the constitution of three types of municipalities in every state.

4. It consists of provisions from Articles 243-P to 243-ZG.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 3, and 4 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **74th Amendment Act of 1992** added a new **Part IX-A** to the **Constitution of India**, which is titled as **'The Municipalities'**. This part constitutionalized the system of **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The Act added the **12th Schedule** to the **Constitution**, not the 10th Schedule. The **12th Schedule** contains **18 functional items** of **municipalities** such as urban planning, regulation of land use, and water supply. The **10th Schedule** is related to the **Anti-Defection Law** added by the **52nd Amendment Act**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The Act provides for the constitution of three types of **municipalities** in every state: a **Nagar Panchayat** for transitional areas, a **Municipal Council** for a smaller urban area, and a **Municipal Corporation** for a larger urban area. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The provisions of this Act are contained in **Articles 243-P to 243-ZG**. These articles detail the **composition**, **reservation of seats**, **duration**, and **powers** of the **municipalities**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Background:** The **74th Constitutional Amendment Act** was passed in **1992** during the tenure of **Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao**. It came into force on **June 1, 1993**. Before this, **urban local bodies** did not have a uniform constitutional status across **India**.
 
• **Types of Municipalities:**
 
 
• **Nagar Panchayat:** Established for an area in transition from a **rural area** to an **urban area**.
 
• **Municipal Council:** Established for a **smaller urban area**.
 
• **Municipal Corporation:** Established for a **larger urban area**, often found in major cities like **Mumbai**, **Delhi**, and **Kolkata**.
 
 
 
• **Reservation of Seats:** The Act mandates the **reservation of seats** for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in every **municipality** in proportion to their **population**. It also provides for a **mandatory reservation** of not less than **one-third** of the total number of seats for **women**.
 
• **Duration:** Every **municipality** is given a **five-year term** of office from the date of its first meeting. If dissolved earlier, **elections** must be held within **six months** from the date of **dissolution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **State Election Commission:** The **superintendence**, **direction**, and **control** of the preparation of **electoral rolls** and the conduct of all **elections** to the **municipalities** are vested in the **State Election Commission**.
 
• **State Finance Commission:** The **Governor** of a state shall, after every **five years**, constitute a **Finance Commission** to review the **financial position** of the **municipalities** and make recommendations regarding the **distribution of taxes** between the **State** and the **municipalities**.
 
• **Committee for District Planning:** Under **Article 243-ZD**, every state must constitute a **District Planning Committee** to consolidate the plans prepared by the **panchayats** and **municipalities** in the **district**.
 
• **Metropolitan Planning Committee:** Under **Article 243-ZE**, every **metropolitan area** shall have a **Metropolitan Planning Committee** to prepare a draft **development plan** for the **metropolitan area** as a whole.
 
• **12th Schedule Items:** Some of the **18 functional items** include **roads and bridges**, **public health**, **fire services**, **slum improvement**, and **urban poverty alleviation** programs.

questions.question: Maria wants to manage startup programs and services that run automatically when Windows 11 starts. Which Windows utility provides dedicated 'Startup' and 'Services' task for this purpose?

The correct answer is __**MSConfig**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MSConfig**, officially known as the **System Configuration Utility**, is a powerful administrative tool used to troubleshoot the **Windows** startup process and manage how the operating system boots.
 
• It provides a dedicated **Services** tab that lists all the services that start when the computer boots, allowing users to enable or disable them. This is crucial for identifying **third-party services** that might be causing system instability. ***Hence, the statement regarding managing services is correct.***
 
• The utility also contains a **Startup** tab. In older versions of **Windows**, this tab allowed direct management of startup programs; however, in **Windows 10** and **Windows 11**, this tab provides a direct link to the **Task Manager** to manage these applications. ***Hence, the statement regarding managing startup programs is correct.***
 
• One of its primary functions is to facilitate a **Clean Boot**. By disabling all non-Microsoft services and startup items via **MSConfig**, users can determine if **background applications** are interfering with **Windows 11** performance or specific software installations.
 
• The tool was first introduced by **Microsoft** in **Windows 98** and has been a staple in every version since, including **Windows XP**, **Windows 7**, **Windows 10**, and **Windows 11**. It is located in the **C:\Windows\System32** directory and can be launched by typing **"msconfig"** in the **Run** dialog box (**Win + R**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Windows Defender (Microsoft Defender Antivirus):**

 
 
• It is the built-in **security software** for **Windows 11** that provides real-time protection against **malware**, **viruses**, and **ransomware**.
 
• It operates as part of the **Windows Security** suite and does not have the primary function of managing general **startup programs** or system **services** for troubleshooting.
 
 
 
• **Disk Cleanup:**
 
 
• This is a **maintenance utility** designed to free up storage space on the **Hard Disk Drive (HDD)** or **Solid State Drive (SSD)**.
 
• It scans the system for **temporary files**, **setup logs**, **Recycle Bin** contents, and **cached data** that can be safely deleted to improve efficiency. It has no role in managing **startup services**.
 
 
 
• **System Restore:**
 
 
• This is a **recovery tool** that allows users to revert the computer's state (including system files, installed applications, and **Windows Registry**) to a previous point in time, known as a **Restore Point**.
 
• It is used to fix system malfunctions after a **driver update** or **software installation** gone wrong, rather than managing the daily **startup** list.
 
 
 
• **Task Manager:**
 
 
• In **Windows 11**, the **Task Manager** (accessed via **Ctrl + Shift + Esc**) is the modern interface for managing **Startup Apps**.
 
• It provides data on the **"Startup Impact"** of each application, categorized as **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**, helping users optimize their **boot time**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **MSConfig Tabs:** The utility consists of five main tabs: **General** (for selection of boot modes like **Normal**, **Diagnostic**, or **Selective**), **Boot** (to manage **Safe Mode** and boot logs), **Services**, **Startup**, and **Tools** (to launch other administrative utilities).
 
• **Diagnostic Startup:** This feature in **MSConfig** allows **Windows** to start with only basic services and drivers, which is the first step in **advanced troubleshooting** for **OS** errors.
 
• **Number of Services:** A typical **Windows 11** installation may have over **200 services**, and **MSConfig** allows users to **"Hide all Microsoft services"** to focus specifically on third-party software conflicts.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Launch of “One Nation, One Mission: End Plastic Pollution”**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **World Environment Day**, **June 5, 2025**, the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** officially announced the national initiative titled **“One Nation, One Mission: End Plastic Pollution”** to streamline waste management across **India**.
 
• The mission serves as a comprehensive roadmap to eliminate plastic leakage into terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems by the **year 2030**, aligning with **Global Environmental Goals** and the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)** mandates.
 
• This initiative integrates all **28 States** and **8 Union Territories** under a single regulatory framework to ensure uniformity in the enforcement of plastic bans and recycling protocols, moving away from fragmented state-level policies.

questions.question: The book “Poverty and Un-British Rule in India”, which compiled evidence from British official sources to explain India’s economic drain, was authored by whom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was the distinguished author of the book **“Poverty and Un-British Rule in India”**, which was published in the **year** **1901**.
 
• The book is famous for providing a systematic and evidence-based explanation of the **economic drain** of wealth from **India** to **Britain** during the colonial period.
 
• He used the term **"Un-British"** to highlight that the exploitative **economic policies** practiced in **India** were contrary to the fair and democratic traditions of the **British** system in their own **country**.
 
• Naoroji was the **first person** to make an attempt to estimate the **national income** of **India**. In the **year** **1867-68**, he calculated the per capita income of **Indians** to be **Rs. 20** per **year**.
 
• The primary **features** of his work included the **“Drain of Wealth”** theory, which argued that **Britain** was siphoning off **India's** resources through taxes, salaries, and trade without giving any equivalent economic return.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**:

 
 
• He was a moderate leader of the **Indian National Congress** and served as its **President** in **1905** during the **Banaras session**.
 
• Known as the political mentor of **Mahatma Gandhi**, he founded the **Servants of India Society** in **1905** to train **Indians** to devote their lives to the cause of the **country**.
 
 
 
• **R. C. Dutt (Romesh Chunder Dutt)**:
 
 
• He was a retired **ICS officer** and a contemporary of Naoroji who also focused on **economic history**.
 
• He authored the influential book **“The Economic History of India”** in **two volumes** (published in **1902** and **1904**), which provided a detailed **survey** of the **economic impact** of **British** rule.
 
 
 
• **M. G. Ranade (Mahadev Govind Ranade)**:
 
 
• Commonly known as the **“Father of Indian Economics”**, he was a founding member of the **Indian National Congress** and a judge of the **Bombay High Court**.
 
• His **applications** of economic theory to the **Indian** context were compiled in the book **“Essays on Indian Economics”**, published in **1898**.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji's Political Career**:
 
 
• He earned the **designation** of the **“Grand Old Man of India”** for his long-standing service to the national movement.
 
• He was the first **Indian** to be elected as a **Member of Parliament (MP)** in the **British** **House of Commons**, representing **Finsbury Central** from **1892** to **1895**.
 
• He served as the **President** of the **Indian National Congress** on **three** occasions: **1886**, **1893**, and **1906**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Drain of Wealth** occurred through several channels, most notably the **“Home Charges”**, which included **interest on public debt**, **pensions** for **British** officials, and **military expenses** incurred in **England**.
 
• The **East India Association** was founded by Naoroji in **London** in the **year** **1866** to lobby **British** **Parliament** members and the public about **Indian** grievances.
 
• The **facts** and **data** presented by Naoroji in his book were revolutionary at the **time** because they used the **British** government's own **statistical reports** to prove the impoverishment of **India**.
 
• In the **Calcutta session** of **1906**, under the presidency of **Dadabhai Naoroji**, the **Indian National Congress** explicitly adopted **“Swaraj”** (Self-government) as its political goal for the first **time**.

questions.question:
Which option correctly completes the general word equation for a neutralisation reaction?

Base + Acid → ________ + ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt + Water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **neutralisation reaction** is a fundamental chemical process where an **acid** and a **base** react quantitatively with each other to produce **salt** and **water**.
 
• In this specific chemical interaction, the **hydrogen ions (H+)** provided by the **acid** react with the **hydroxide ions (OH-)** provided by the **base** to form **water (H2O)** molecules.
 
• The **salt** produced in the reaction is an **ionic compound** formed from the **cation** (positive ion) of the base and the **anion** (negative ion) of the acid.
 
• The general word equation representing this process is: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**. This equation represents the elimination of acidic and basic properties of the reactants.
 
• These reactions are typically **exothermic** in nature, meaning **heat energy** is released into the surroundings during the formation of the products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Acids and Bases:**

 
 
• **Acids** are substances that release **hydrogen ions (H+)** in aqueous solutions and have a **pH** value ranging from **0 to 6.9**. Examples include **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)**.
 
• **Bases** are substances that release **hydroxide ions (OH-)** in aqueous solutions and have a **pH** value ranging from **7.1 to 14**. Examples include **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)**.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Salt:**
 
 
• The type of **salt** formed depends on the specific **acid** and **base** used. For example, the reaction between **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** yields **Sodium chloride (NaCl)**, commonly known as **table salt**.
 
• The reaction between **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)** and **Calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2)** produces **Calcium sulfate (CaSO4)**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications of Neutralisation:**
 
 
• **Agriculture:** If the **soil** is too **acidic**, farmers treat it with **bases** like **quick lime (Calcium oxide)** or **slaked lime (Calcium hydroxide)** to ensure optimal **pH** for crop growth.
 
• **Medicine:** To treat **indigestion** caused by excess **Hydrochloric acid** in the stomach, patients take **antacids** such as **Milk of Magnesia (Magnesium hydroxide)**, which is a mild **base**.
 
• **Waste Treatment:** Industrial **effluents** containing **acids** are neutralized with **basic chemicals** before being released into **water bodies** to prevent environmental damage.
 
• **Biological Stings:** An **ant sting** injects **formic acid** into the skin, which can be neutralized by rubbing **moist baking soda (Sodium hydrogen carbonate)** or **calamine solution** (containing **Zinc carbonate**) on the affected area.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indicators:** To identify the completion of a **neutralisation reaction**, chemical **indicators** like **Phenolphthalein** or **Methyl orange** are used. In a **titration**, the **end-point** is reached when the **acid** is completely neutralized by the **base**, often indicated by a **color change**.
 
• **pH Scale:** The concept of the **pH scale** was introduced by **S.P.L. Sorensen** in **1909**. A **neutral solution** (like pure water) has a **pH** value of **7** at **25 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Strength of Reactants:**
 
 
• Reaction between a **strong acid** and a **strong base** results in a **neutral salt (pH 7)**.
 
• Reaction between a **strong acid** and a **weak base** results in an **acidic salt (pH 7)**.

Numerical value of Area = 2 × Numerical value of Perimeter

Perimeter of circle (P) = 2πr

**Calculations:**

Let the radius of the circle be r units.

⇒ Area = πr²

⇒ Perimeter = 2πr

According to the given condition:

⇒ πr² = 2 × (2πr)

⇒ πr² = 4πr

⇒ r = 4 units

⇒ Diameter (D) = 2 × r

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 4 = 8 units

Exactly half of the circle area: A = (1/2)πr².

questions.question: The Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019, provides citizenship to individuals belonging to which communities if they entered India before 31st December 2014 from Pakistan or Afghanistan or Bangladesh?

options.text: Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, Christian

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, Christian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019** (**CAA**) aims to provide Indian citizenship to persecuted religious minorities from three specific neighboring countries.
 
• The Act specifically applies to individuals belonging to **six communities**: **Hindu**, **Sikh**, **Buddhist**, **Jain**, **Parsi**, and **Christian**. These groups are considered minorities in their respective home countries of **Pakistan**, **Afghanistan**, and **Bangladesh**.
 
• To be eligible under this Act, the individuals must have entered **India** on or before the cut-off date of **31st December 2014**.
 
• The **Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019**, amends the **Citizenship Act, 1955**, to facilitate a faster path to citizenship for these specific groups by reducing the residency requirement for **naturalization**.
 
• Under the new provisions, the requirement of residence in **India** for these individuals has been reduced from **11 years** to just **5 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Exemptions for Tribal Areas:** The provisions of the **Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019** do not apply to tribal areas of **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, **Mizoram**, or **Tripura** as included in the **Sixth Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• **Inner Line Permit (ILP):** The **CAA** also excludes areas regulated under the **Inner Line Permit** system. This currently includes the states of **Arunachal Pradesh**, **Nagaland**, **Manipur**, and **Mizoram**. This is to protect the distinct cultural and indigenous identity of these regions.
 
• **Legal Status:** Before this amendment, "illegal migrants" were prohibited from acquiring **Indian citizenship**. The **2019 Act** ensures that the defined six communities from the three countries will no longer be treated as illegal migrants for the purpose of the **Citizenship Act**.
 
• **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI):** The Act also contains provisions regarding the cancellation of **OCI** registration if the cardholder violates any law notified by the **Central Government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Notification of Rules:** Although the **Parliament of India** passed the bill in **December 2019**, the **Ministry of Home Affairs** (**MHA**) officially notified the **Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2024**, on **11th March 2024**.
 
• **Constitutional Framework:** Matters related to **citizenship** in **India** are governed by **Articles 5 to 11** under **Part II** of the **Constitution of India**. However, these articles do not provide a permanent law; the **Parliament** has the power under **Article 11** to regulate the right of citizenship by law.
 
• **Application Process:** The application for citizenship under **CAA** is handled through an **online portal**, and the entire process is designed to be **digital** to ensure transparency and efficiency.
 
• **Designated Authority:** The **Empowered Committee** headed by the **Director (Census Operations)** of the state or Union Territory concerned is the final authority to grant citizenship under these rules.

questions.question:
By selling an article at (2)/(5) of its actual selling price, Akash incurs a loss of 24%.

If he sells it at 84% of its actual selling price, then the profit percentage is
questions.solution:

2/5 of Actual Selling Price (ASP) = 100% − 24% = 76% of CP.

⇒ Actual SP = 76% × 5 ÷ 2 = 190% of CP.

New Selling Price = 84% of Actual SP = 84% × 190% of CP.

⇒ New SP = 0.84 × 190% = 159.6% of CP.

Profit % = 159.6% − 100% = 59.6%.

**∴ Answer = 59.6%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Loss = 24% when SP = 2/5 of Actual SP. Target SP = 84% of Actual SP.

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100 | Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 
• CP = 100 New SP = 159.6 Actual SP = 190 
 Profit: 59.6% 
• 2/5 ASP = 76 

**Calculations:**

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100 units.

⇒ If Loss = 24%, then Selling Price (SP₁) = 100 − 24 = 76 units.

⇒ Given SP₁ = 2/5 × Actual SP.

⇒ 76 = 2/5 × Actual SP ⇒ Actual SP = (76 × 5) ÷ 2 = 190 units.

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = 84% of Actual SP = 0.84 × 190.

⇒ New SP₂ = 159.6 units.

⇒ Profit = SP₂ − CP = 159.6 − 100 = 59.6 units.

⇒ Profit % = (59.6 ÷ 100) × 100 = 59.6%.

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, net change = [a + b + (a × b)/100]%.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − Discount%)/100. Also, CP × (100 + P%) = MP × (100 − D%).

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100. Profit/Loss is always calculated on Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

questions.question: The population of a village was 2,90,000. It increased by 15% in the first year and increased by 25% in the second year. Its population after two years is _______.

Net change = 15 + 25 + (15 × 25 ÷ 100) = 40 + 3.75 = 43.75%

Increase in 1st year (r₁) = 15%

Increase in 2nd year (r₂) = 25%

 2,90,000 Initial 
 
 +15% 3,33,500 Year 1 
 +25% 4,16,875 Year 2 Total Growth = 43.75%

Population after 1st year = 2,90,000 × (1 + 15/100)

questions.question: 100 men have provisions for 26 days. If 60 men have left, for how many days the same provisions would last for the remaining men?

Initial number of men (M₁) = 100

Initial number of days (D₁) = 26

Number of men who left = 60

**Formula used:**

Total Work (Provision) = LCM of all given days (or M₁ × D₁)

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days

 
 

 **Person**

 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 100 Men

 D₂

Remaining men = 100 − 60 = 40

New Days = 2600 ÷ 40 = 65 days

**Calculations:**

Total provision = M₁ × D₁ = 100 × 26 = 2600 units

⇒ Number of remaining men (M₂) = 100 − 60 = 40

⇒ New duration (D₂) = Total provision ÷ M₂

questions.question: A dealer buys two articles X and Y for ₹500 each. He marks each of them at the same price. He sells X by giving two successive discounts of 20% and 45% and still earns ₹636 as profit. If he sells Y at a single discount of 67%, then what is the profit percentage on Y?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SP of X = 500 + 636 = 1136

Net multiplier for X (20% & 45% discount) = 0.80 × 0.55 = 0.44

Multiplier for Y (67% discount) = 1 − 0.67 = 0.33

SP of Y = (0.33 ÷ 0.44) × 1136 = (3/4) × 1136 = 852

Profit % on Y = [(852 − 500) ÷ 500] × 100 = 70.4%

**∴ Answer = 70.4%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of X and Y = ₹500 each. Profit on X = ₹636. Discounts on X = 20% and 45%. Discount on Y = 67%.

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit | SP = MP × (100 − D%)/100 | Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
• CP (500) MP SP X (1136) SP Y (852) 
 56% Dis 
 67% Dis 

**Calculations:**

SP of article X = CP + Profit = 500 + 636 = ₹1136

⇒ Effective discount on X = 20 + 45 − (20 × 45 ÷ 100) = 65 − 9 = 56%

⇒ SP of X = MP × (100 − 56)% = 0.44 × MP

⇒ 1136 = 0.44 × MP ⇒ MP = 1136 ÷ 0.44

⇒ SP of article Y (at 67% discount) = MP × (100 − 67)% = 0.33 × MP

⇒ SP of Y = 0.33 × (1136 ÷ 0.44) = 1136 × (3 ÷ 4) = ₹852

⇒ Profit on Y = SP of Y − CP = 852 − 500 = ₹352

⇒ Profit % on Y = (352 ÷ 500) × 100 = 70.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 70.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

Total Discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

Profit Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100. It is always calculated on the base of Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price and Selling Price

Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount. Also, SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

For multiple changes, net multiplier = m₁ × m₂ × ... × mₙ. For example, 20% discount is a multiplier of 0.80.

questions.question: Who is credited with the discovery of the electron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**J.J. Thomson**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **J.J. Thomson**, a **British physicist**, is universally credited with the discovery of the **electron** in the year **1897**.
 
• The discovery was made through his experiments with **cathode ray tubes (CRT)**, where he observed that the rays were deflected by **electric** and **magnetic fields**, indicating they were composed of **negatively charged particles**.
 
• He initially named these particles **"corpuscles,"** but the name was later changed to **"electron,"** a term proposed by **George Johnstone Stoney** in **1891**.
 
• **Thomson** succeeded in measuring the **charge-to-mass ratio (e/m)** of the electron, which proved that these particles were much smaller than the **Hydrogen atom** and were fundamental constituents of all atoms.
 
• For his theoretical and experimental investigations on the **conduction of electricity by gases** and the subsequent discovery of the electron, **J.J. Thomson** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1906**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ernest Rutherford:**

 
 
• Known as the **"father of nuclear physics,"** he discovered the **atomic nucleus** in **1911** through the famous **Alpha Ray Scattering Experiment** (or **Gold Foil Experiment**).
 
• He is also credited with the discovery of the **proton** in **1917** and the concept of **radioactive half-life**.
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in **1908** for his investigations into the disintegration of elements and the chemistry of **radioactive substances**.
 
 
 
• **Marie Curie:**
 
 
• A **Polish-French physicist** and chemist who conducted pioneering research on **radioactivity**.
 
• She discovered the elements **Polonium** (named after her native country, Poland) and **Radium** in **1898**.
 
• She remains the only person to win **Nobel Prizes** in two different scientific categories: **Physics (1903)** and **Chemistry (1911)**.
 
 
 
• **Albert Einstein:**
 
 
• A **German-born theoretical physicist** famous for developing the **Theory of Relativity** (Special and General).
 
• He formulated the mass-energy equivalence equation **E=mc²**, which is considered the world's most famous equation.
 
• He received the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1921** for his services to theoretical physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the **photoelectric effect**.
 
 
 
• **James Chadwick:**
 
 
• He was a **British physicist** who discovered the **neutron** in **1932**, a subatomic particle with no electrical charge located in the nucleus.
 
• This discovery was crucial for the development of **nuclear fission** and the **atomic bomb**. He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1935**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atomic Models:** Following the discovery of the electron, **J.J. Thomson** proposed the **"Plum Pudding Model"** of the atom, where negatively charged electrons were embedded in a uniform sphere of positive charge.
 
• **Electron Properties:** The **electron** carries a negative **elementary charge** of approximately **-1.602 x 10⁻¹⁹ Coulombs**. Its **rest mass** is approximately **9.109 x 10⁻³¹ kilograms**.
 
• **Subatomic Timeline:**
 
 
• **1897:** Discovery of **Electron** by **J.J. Thomson**.
 
• **1911/1917:** Discovery of **Nucleus/Proton** by **Ernest Rutherford**.
 
• **1932:** Discovery of **Neutron** by **James Chadwick**.
 
 
 
• **Applications:** The understanding of electrons is fundamental to **electronics**, **electricity**, **chemistry** (bonding), and technologies such as **Electron Microscopes** and **Particle Accelerators**.

questions.question: What action did the Supreme Court take regarding mining near national parks and wildlife sanctuaries on November 13, 2025?

options.text: Banned mining activities within one km

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banned mining activities within one km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India has mandated that every **protected forest**, **national park**, and **wildlife sanctuary** across the **country** must have a mandatory **Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ)** of a minimum of **one kilometre** starting from their demarcated boundaries.
 
• As per the judicial directive, **mining activities** are strictly **prohibited** within the **national parks** and **wildlife sanctuaries**, and this ban extends to the **1 km** **buffer zone** or **ESZ**.
 
• This decision was primarily influenced by the landmark **T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad vs. Union of India** case, which focuses on the conservation of forest land and **biodiversity**.
 
• The court also ruled that no **permanent structures** can be built within the **ESZ**, ensuring that the area acts as a "shock absorber" for the **environment** and prevents human encroachment into **fragile ecosystems**.
 
• The **Supreme Court** emphasized that the **state** must act as a trustee of the **natural resources** and ensure the **protection** of **wildlife** for future generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs):**

 
 
• These are **ecologically fragile areas** notified by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** around **Protected Areas**.
 
• The **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** serves as the legal framework for declaring these zones.
 
• The main **objective** of **ESZs** is to regulate human **activities** in the vicinity of **National Parks** and **Wildlife Sanctuaries** to minimize negative impacts on the **ecosystem**.
 
 
 
• **National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries:**
 
 
• A **National Park** is an area with a high level of **protection** where no human activity or private **land ownership** is allowed under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**.
 
• **Wildlife Sanctuaries** are areas where some human activities, such as **grazing** or **resource collection**, may be permitted as long as they do not interfere with the well-being of the **animals**.
 
• India currently has over **100 National Parks** and more than **500 Wildlife Sanctuaries**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• Activities in these zones are classified into three categories: **Prohibited** (e.g., **commercial mining**, polluting industries), **Regulated** (e.g., felling of trees), and **Permitted** (e.g., **organic farming**, rainwater harvesting).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implementation:** The **Chief Wildlife Warden** of each **state** or **union territory** is responsible for preparing a list of all existing **structures** within the **ESZ** and submitting a **report** to the **Supreme Court**.
 
• **Exceptions:** In cases where the **statutory threshold** of **one kilometre** is difficult to maintain due to existing **habitats** or **geographic** constraints, the **Supreme Court** provides a mechanism for **state governments** to approach the **Central Empowered Committee (CEC)** for **modifications**.
 
• **Impact of Mining:** **Mining** near **protected areas** leads to **habitat fragmentation**, **noise pollution**, and **water contamination**, which severely affects the **flora** and **fauna** of the region.
 
• **Judicial Oversight:** The **Supreme Court** has consistently used the **Public Trust Doctrine** to ensure that **environmental protection** takes precedence over **commercial interests** such as **mining** and **quarrying**.

questions.question:
How many solutions for given three unknowns are possible to satisfy all these equations?

-3alpha + 2beta + -5gamma = -14

2alpha - 3beta + 4gamma = 10

alpha + beta + gamma = 4
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum all three equations: (−3 + 2 + 1)α + (2 − 3 + 1)β + (−5 + 4 + 1)γ = −14 + 10 + 4

Simplifying the sum: 0α + 0β + 0γ = 0 ⇒ 0 = 0

Since the sum results in 0 = 0, the equations are linearly dependent and consistent.

With 3 variables and only 2 independent equations, the system has infinitely many solutions.

**∴ Answer = Infinite solutions**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Eq 1: −3α + 2β − 5γ = −14

Eq 2: 2α − 3β + 4γ = 10

Eq 3: α + β + γ = 4

**Formula used:**

Consistency Rule: If the determinant of coefficients (D) is 0 and all minor determinants (Dα, Dβ, Dγ) are 0, the system has infinite solutions.

 
• 
 
 
 Plane 1 (Eq 1) Plane 2 (Eq 2) Plane 3 (Eq 3) Infinite Solutions (Line) 

**Calculations:**

Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ (−3α + 2α) + (2β − 3β) + (−5γ + 4γ) = −14 + 10

⇒ −α − β − γ = −4

⇒ α + β + γ = 4

⇒ Observe that this result is identical to Eq 3.

⇒ This means Equation 3 is redundant. We only have 2 independent linear equations for 3 variables.

⇒ Since the equations are consistent and have a free variable, there are infinite solutions.

**∴ The correct answer is (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unique Solution Condition

A system of linear equations has a unique solution if the determinant of the coefficient matrix is non-zero (D ≠ 0).

No Solution (Inconsistent)

A system has no solution if the determinant D = 0, but at least one of the minor determinants (Dα, Dβ, or Dγ) is non-zero.

Infinite Solutions (Geometrical Meaning)

For three variables, infinite solutions occur when the three planes intersect in a common line or are all the same plane.

Cramer's Rule

A method using determinants to solve systems of linear equations where α = Dα÷D, β = Dβ÷D, and γ = Dγ÷D.

questions.question: Which layer of the Earth plays the primary role in generating the planet’s magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Outer core**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Outer core** is the layer of the Earth primarily responsible for generating the **magnetic field** through a process called the **Geodynamo**. This layer is situated at a **depth** of approximately **2,900 kilometers** to **5,150 kilometers** below the Earth's surface.
 
• It is composed mainly of **liquid iron** and **nickel**. Unlike the inner core, the outer core remains in a **liquid state** because the **temperature** (ranging from **4,000°C to 6,000°C**) is high enough to overcome the **pressure** at that depth.
 
• The **rotation** of the Earth, combined with **convection currents** in the liquid metal, causes the movement of **electrically conducting** fluids. This movement creates **electrical currents**, which in turn generate the **geomagnetic field**.
 
• This magnetic field extends from the Earth's interior out into space, where it interacts with the **solar wind** to form the **magnetosphere**. This is vital for protecting the **atmosphere** from **harmful radiation**.
 
• The **thickness** of the outer core is roughly **2,200 kilometers**, making it a massive reservoir of **kinetic energy** converted into **magnetic energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Crust:**

 
 
• The **Crust** is the **outermost solid shell** of the Earth. It ranges in **thickness** from about **5 kilometers** (under oceans) to **70 kilometers** (under mountain ranges).
 
• It is primarily composed of **silicates** and **aluminum** (Sial) and **silicates** and **magnesium** (Sima). While it contains some **magnetic minerals** like magnetite, it does not generate the global magnetic field. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Mantle:**
 
 
• The **Mantle** lies beneath the crust and extends to a **depth** of about **2,900 kilometers**. It makes up about **84%** of the Earth's total **volume**.
 
• It consists of **solid rock** that behaves like a **viscous fluid** over **geological time**. While convection in the mantle drives **plate tectonics**, it does not possess the **electrical conductivity** required to generate a magnetic field. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Inner core:**

questions.question: The abbreviation BIOS stands for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basic Input/Output System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The abbreviation **BIOS** stands for **Basic Input/Output System**. It is a critical piece of **firmware** that is pre-installed on a personal computer's **motherboard** and is the first software to run when the machine is powered on.
 
• The primary function of the **BIOS** is to manage the communication between the **Operating System (OS)** and the hardware components such as the **Hard Drive**, **Video Adapter**, **Keyboard**, **Mouse**, and **Printer**.
 
• Upon starting the computer, the **BIOS** performs a diagnostic routine known as the **Power-On Self-Test (POST)**. This process checks if the system's hardware, including the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **Random Access Memory (RAM)**, and **Storage Devices**, are functioning correctly before handng over control to the **Bootloader**.
 
• It contains a **Bootstrap Loader**, which is a small program responsible for locating the **Operating System** on the **Hard Drive** or **SSD** and loading it into the **System Memory** to initiate the user environment.
 
• The **BIOS** is typically stored on a **Non-volatile ROM (Read-Only Memory)** chip, such as an **EPROM** or **Flash Memory**, ensuring that the instructions are not lost when the power is turned off.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface)**: Modern computers have largely replaced the traditional **Legacy BIOS** with **UEFI**. **UEFI** supports larger **Hard Drives** (greater than **2.2 Terabytes**), offers faster **Boot Times**, provides a **Graphical User Interface (GUI)** with mouse support, and includes **Secure Boot** features to prevent malware from loading during startup.
 
• **CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor)**: While the **BIOS** software is stored in **ROM**, the user-defined settings (such as **System Time**, **Date**, and **Boot Priority**) are stored in a small amount of **RAM** called the **CMOS chip**. This chip is kept active by a small **CMOS Battery** (usually a **CR2032 Lithium coin cell**) even when the computer is unplugged.
 
• **History and Origin**: The term **BIOS** was first coined by **Gary Kildall** in **1975**. It was originally part of the **CP/M operating system**, describing the hardware-specific part of the system that loaded during boot and interacted directly with the hardware.
 
• **Flashing the BIOS**: To fix bugs or add support for new hardware (like a newer generation **Processor**), the **BIOS** can be updated through a process called **Flashing**. This involves overwriting the existing **Firmware** with a newer version provided by the **Motherboard Manufacturer**.
 
• **Accessibility**: Users can access the **BIOS Setup Utility** during the early stages of booting by pressing specific keys, commonly **F2**, **F10**, **F12**, or **Delete**, depending on the manufacturer like **Dell**, **HP**, or **ASUS**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Firmware vs Software**: It is important to distinguish that **BIOS** is **Firmware**, meaning it is low-level code embedded directly into a hardware chip, whereas an **Operating System** like **Windows 11** or **Linux** is high-level **Software**.
 
• **Hardware Initialization**: Without a functioning **BIOS**, a computer would not know how to "wake up" its hardware components or where to find the **Operating System**, rendering the device a "brick."
 
• **Drivers**: In the early days of computing, the **BIOS** provided the primary **Drivers** for hardware; however, in modern systems, the **Operating System** loads its own advanced **Device Drivers** after the initial boot process is complete.

questions.question: In Windows 11, a file with the .msi file extension is primarily designed for which specific function?

options.text: Storing formatted Text, Image and Document content
Encoding multimedia audio and video streams
Executing the installation of software applications

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Executing the installation of software applications**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **.msi** file extension stands for **Microsoft Installer**, which is now formally known as the **Windows Installer**. Its primary purpose in **Windows 11** and earlier versions is to manage the **installation**, **maintenance**, and **removal** of software.
 
• An **.msi** file functions as a **relational database** package. It contains all the necessary information, such as **files**, **registry keys**, **component relationships**, and **shortcuts**, required to install a specific piece of **software**.
 
• When a user double-clicks an **.msi** file, the **Windows Installer service** (msiexec.exe) is triggered to read the package and execute the defined **installation scripts**.
 
• One of the most critical features of the **.msi** format is its **transactional** nature. If an **installation** fails midway, the **Windows Installer** can perform a **rollback**, returning the **system** to its original state before the process began.
 
• In **corporate environments**, **.msi** files are preferred because they support **silent installations** and can be easily deployed across multiple **computers** using **Group Policy Objects (GPO)** or **Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Comparison with .exe files:** While both **.msi** and **.exe** can be used for **installation**, an **.exe** is a generic **executable** file that may contain its own setup engine. In contrast, an **.msi** file specifically relies on the **Windows Installer engine** built into the **operating system**.
 
• **MSIX format in Windows 11:** With the release of **Windows 10** and **Windows 11**, **Microsoft** introduced the **.msix** format. It is a modern **packaging format** that combines the best features of **MSI**, **AppX**, and **App-V** to provide a more secure and reliable **application** deployment experience.
 
• **Multimedia and Image Formats:** Other extensions mentioned in the options serve different purposes. For example, **.mp4** or **.mkv** are used for **multimedia audio and video**, while **.psd** or **.svg** are used for **raster and vector images**. These are not related to **software installation**.
 
• **Uninstallation and Repair:** Because **.msi** files track every change made to the **Windows Registry** and **file system**, they allow users to **repair** a corrupted installation or perform a clean **uninstallation** through the **Control Panel** or **Settings** app.
 
• **Customization:** Developers can use **MST (Microsoft Transform)** files along with an **.msi** to customize the **installation** process for different groups of users without modifying the original **installer package**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Security:** Since **.msi** files can execute **scripts** and modify **system files**, **Windows 11** uses **User Account Control (UAC)** to prompt for **administrator permissions** before allowing the **installation** to proceed.
 
• **Version History:** The **Windows Installer** was first introduced in **1999** with **Office 2000** and has since become the standard for **Windows** software distribution.
 
• **Deployment:** The **.msi** format is highly **standardized**, ensuring that **software vendors** provide a predictable **user experience** during the **setup** process regardless of the **hardware** or specific **Windows** build.

Value = −18.

**∴ The correct answer is -18.**

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a moderately skewed distribution, the difference between Mode and Median is exactly twice the difference between Median and Mean.

Logic: (Mode − Median) = 2 × (Median − Mean)

Given: Mode − Median = 77.74

Calculation: Median − Mean = 77.74 ÷ 2 = 38.87

**∴ Answer = 38.87**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Mode − Median = 77.74

**Formula used:**

Empirical Formula: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean

 
• Mean Median Mode 
 Mode − Median = 77.74 
 x = ? Relationship: (Mode − Median) = 2 × (Median − Mean) 77.74 = 2 × x 

**Calculations:**

Using the empirical relation: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean

⇒ Subtracting Median from both sides:

⇒ Mode − Median = 3 Median − 2 Mean − Median

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 Median − 2 Mean

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 × (Median − Mean)

⇒ 77.74 = 2 × (Median − Mean)

⇒ Median − Mean = 77.74 ÷ 2

⇒ Median − Mean = 38.87

**∴ The correct answer is 38.87.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean. This is also written as (Mean − Mode) = 3(Mean − Median).

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution (like the Normal Distribution), the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness and the Median

The Median always lies between the Mean and the Mode in a skewed distribution. It is a more robust measure of central tendency than the Mean for skewed data.

Types of Skewness

Positively skewed: Mean > Median > Mode. Negatively skewed: Mode > Median > Mean.

questions.question: At what rate (in percentage, rounded off to two decimal place) per year will a sum of money 5 times itself in 22 years on simple interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes n times in T years, Rate R = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T

Here, n = 5 and T = 22 years

R = [(5 − 1) × 100] ÷ 22

R = 400 ÷ 22 = 18.1818...

**∴ Answer = 18.18**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Principal becomes 5 times itself (Amount A = 5P). Time T = 22 years.

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• Year 0 Principal (P) Year 22 Amount (5P) 
 Interest = 4P 

**Calculations:**

Let Principal (P) = 100

⇒ Amount (A) = 5 × 100 = 500

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) = A − P = 500 − 100 = 400

⇒ 400 = (100 × R × 22) ÷ 100

⇒ 400 = 22 × R

⇒ R = 400 ÷ 22 = 18.1818...

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18 (Option 3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Amount Formula

Total Amount A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100], where P is Principal, R is Rate, and T is Time.

Time for n times

To find the time (T) required for a sum to become n times at rate R, use T = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ R.

SI vs CI difference

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given by CI − SI = P × (R ÷ 100)².
