questions.question: Which plant tissue is responsible for transporting water from the roots to the leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is a specialized type of **vascular tissue** in **tracheophytes** (vascular plants) that is primarily responsible for the **conduction of water** and **dissolved minerals** from the **roots** to the **stems** and **leaves**.
 
• The transport in **xylem** is **unidirectional**, meaning the movement of substances occurs only in the upward direction, from the **bottom to the top** of the plant.
 
• It provides **mechanical strength** to the plant body due to the presence of **lignified cell walls** in its components.
 
• The **xylem** consists of four main types of cells: **Tracheids**, **Vessels** (also known as trachea), **Xylem Parenchyma**, and **Xylem Fibres**.
 
• Except for **xylem parenchyma**, all other xylem elements are **dead cells** at maturity, which facilitates the efficient flow of water under high tension.
 
• **Tracheids** and **vessels** are the main **conducting elements**; they are tube-like structures that allow water to move through the plant via **capillary action** and **transpiration pull**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phloem:**

 
 
• **Phloem** is the other major **vascular tissue** responsible for the **translocation of organic nutrients**, especially **sucrose** (sugar), produced during **photosynthesis**.
 
• Unlike xylem, the transport in **phloem** is **bidirectional** (multi-directional), moving food from the **source** (leaves) to the **sink** (roots, fruits, and storage organs).
 
• It is composed of **Sieve tubes**, **Companion cells**, **Phloem parenchyma**, and **Phloem fibres**. Most of these cells are **living** at maturity.
 
 
 
• **Epidermis:**
 
 
• The **Epidermis** is the **outermost layer** of cells covering the entire surface of the plant, including **roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and seeds**.
 
• Its primary **function** is **protection** against **mechanical injury**, **water loss** (via the **cuticle**), and **pathogen entry**.
 
• In leaves, it contains specialized pores called **stomata**, which are regulated by **guard cells** for **gas exchange** and **transpiration**.
 
 
 
• **Cortex:**
 
 
• The **Cortex** is a region of **ground tissue** located between the **epidermis** and the **vascular cylinder** (stele) in **roots** and **stems**.
 
• It is mostly composed of **parenchyma cells** and serves functions like **storage of food** (starch) and **transport of water** and minerals from the epidermis to the vascular center.
 
• In some plants, the innermost layer of the cortex is differentiated into the **endodermis**, which regulates the flow of materials into the xylem.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mechanism of Water Transport:** The movement of water in the **xylem** is driven by two main forces: **Root Pressure** (which pushes water up from the bottom, significant in small plants or at night) and **Transpiration Pull** (which sucks water up from the leaves due to evaporation).
 
• **Ascent of Sap:** The upward movement of water and minerals through the **xylem** is scientifically termed the **Ascent of Sap**. This process is explained by the **Cohesion-Tension Theory**, proposed by **Dixon and Jolly** in **1894**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The term **Xylem** was introduced by **Carl Nägeli** in **1858**, derived from the **Greek word "xylon"**, meaning **wood**, as xylem forms the bulk of the wood in perennial plants.
 
• **Environmental Factors:** The **rate of transport** in the **xylem** is heavily influenced by external factors like **temperature**, **humidity**, **wind speed**, and **light intensity**, as these directly affect the **rate of transpiration**.

questions.question: Which report, released at the COP30 summit in 2025, highlights the rapid increase in global methane emissions and the need for urgent action to address climate change?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Global Methane Status Report 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Methane Status Report 2025** was a landmark document released during the **COP30** summit, which took place in **Belém, Brazil**, in **November 2025**. This report provides a comprehensive assessment of global methane emission trends and the efficacy of current mitigation strategies.
 
• The report highlights that **methane (CH4)** is a powerful greenhouse gas, responsible for approximately **30%** of the total rise in global temperatures since the **Industrial Revolution**. It underscores that while methane has a shorter atmospheric lifespan than CO2, its warming potential is significantly higher.
 
• According to the findings, global methane emissions from human activities must be reduced by nearly **45%** by **2030** to stay within the **1.5°C** warming limit set by the **Paris Agreement**. The 2025 report identified that emissions have continued to rise despite the **Global Methane Pledge** initiated in **2021**.
 
• The **Global Methane Status Report 2025** was jointly prepared by the **International Energy Agency (IEA)** and the **Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC)**, under the auspices of the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)**. It serves as a critical tool for policymakers to identify "super-emitters" and implement targeted regulations.
 
• The report emphasizes the "triple-win" of methane reduction: slowing **climate change**, improving **air quality** by reducing ground-level **ozone**, and enhancing **energy security** through the capture of leaked natural gas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Methane:**

 
 
• **Methane** is the primary component of **natural gas**. It has an atmospheric lifetime of about **12 years**, which is much shorter than **carbon dioxide**, which can persist for centuries.
 
• Despite its short life, its **Global Warming Potential (GWP)** is more than **80 times** that of CO2 over a **20-year** period, making it a "short-lived climate pollutant" (SLCP) with immediate impact.
 
 
 
• **Primary Sources of Emissions:**
 
 
• **Agriculture:** This sector accounts for roughly **40%** of anthropogenic methane, primarily from **livestock enteric fermentation** and **rice cultivation**.
 
• **Energy:** The **oil and gas** industry and **coal mining** contribute about **35%** of emissions through venting, flaring, and fugitive leaks.
 
• **Waste Management:** Landfills and wastewater treatment plants are responsible for approximately **20%** of emissions due to the **anaerobic decomposition** of organic matter.
 
 
 
• **The Global Methane Pledge:**
 
 
• Launched at **COP26** in **Glasgow** (**2021**), this initiative saw over **150 countries** commit to a collective goal of reducing methane emissions by at least **30%** from **2020** levels by the **year 2030**.
 
 
 
• **COP30 Significance:**
 
 
• The **30th Conference of the Parties (COP30)** is often referred to as the "**Amazon COP**" because of its location in **Brazil**. It marks a critical juncture for nations to submit their updated **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** for **2035**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Monitoring Technologies:** The **Global Methane Status Report 2025** utilizes data from advanced satellites like **MethaneSAT** and the **International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO)** to track real-time leaks across the globe.
 
• **Health Impacts:** Reducing methane is vital because it is a precursor to **tropospheric ozone**. Higher ozone levels cause **respiratory illnesses** and lead to the loss of millions of tonnes of **crop yields** annually.
 
• **Economic Viability:** The **IEA** reports that nearly **40%** of methane emissions from fossil fuel operations could be avoided at **no net cost** because the value of the captured gas exceeds the cost of the abatement measures.
 
• **MARS Initiative:** The **Methane Alert and Response System (MARS)** was scaled up by **2025** to provide high-resolution data to governments to fix large leaks immediately, a feature highlighted as a success in the 2025 report.

questions.question: What is the ratio between fourth proportional of 10, 80, 30 and fourth proportional of 7, 28, 19?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Fourth proportional (D) = (B × C) ÷ A

For (10, 80, 30): D₁ = (80 × 30) ÷ 10 = 240

For (7, 28, 19): D₂ = (28 × 19) ÷ 7 = 76

Required Ratio = 240 : 76 = 60 : 19

**∴ Answer = 60:19**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Set 1: 10, 80, 30

Set 2: 7, 28, 19

**Formula used:**

If a, b, c, d are in proportion, then a/b = c/d ⇒ d = (b × c) / a

 Set 1 (10, 80, 30, x) 10 : 80 :: 30 : x x = 240 Set 2 (7, 28, 19, y) 7 : 28 :: 19 : y y = 76 
• Ratio x : y = 240 : 76 = 60 : 19 

**Calculations:**

Let x be the fourth proportional of 10, 80, 30.

⇒ 10/80 = 30/x

⇒ 1/8 = 30/x ⇒ x = 30 × 8 = 240

Let y be the fourth proportional of 7, 28, 19.

⇒ 7/28 = 19/y

⇒ 1/4 = 19/y ⇒ y = 19 × 4 = 76

Required Ratio = x : y = 240 : 76

⇒ Ratio = (240 ÷ 4) : (76 ÷ 4) = 60 : 19

**∴ The correct answer is 60:19 (Option 4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportional

The third proportional of a and b is the value c such that a:b = b:c, calculated as c = b² ÷ a.

Invertendo and Alternendo

If a:b = c:d, then b:a = d:c (Invertendo) and a:c = b:d (Alternendo).

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a:b is a² : b², while the sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

questions.question: The Taiga Type region is best described as which major natural region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coniferous Forests Region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Taiga Type region** is characterized by its vast expanse of **coniferous forests**, which consist primarily of **needle-leaved evergreen trees**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• It is the **world's largest land biome**, making up nearly **29%** of the world’s forest cover. It is also widely known as the **Boreal Forest** in North America.
 
• The region is predominantly located in the **high latitudes** of the **Northern Hemisphere**, specifically between **50°N and 70°N**. It is absent in the Southern Hemisphere due to the lack of large landmasses at those latitudes.
 
• The climate of the Taiga is characterized by **extremely long, cold winters** and **short, cool summers**. The **annual temperature range** is the highest among all biomes, with temperatures dropping as low as **-54°C** in winter and reaching **30°C** in summer.
 
• The term **'Taiga'** is a **Russian** word that refers to a **marshy pine forest** or a **vast coniferous forest**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Distribution:** The Taiga belt stretches across **Northern Russia (Siberia)**, **Canada**, **Alaska**, and parts of **Scandinavia** (Norway, Sweden, and Finland).
 
• **Vegetation Characteristics:** The dominant flora includes **Evergreen Conifers** such as **Spruce**, **Fir**, and **Pine**. These trees have a **conical shape** to allow snow to slide off easily and **needle-like leaves** with a thick **waxy cuticle** to minimize **transpiration** and survive **frost**.
 
• **Soil Type:** The soils in this region are known as **Podzols**. They are typically **acidic**, **ash-grey** in color, and **nutrient-poor** because the cold climate slows down the **decomposition** of organic matter.
 
• **Economic Importance:** The Taiga is the primary source of **softwood** in the world. **Lumbering** is a major industry, and the wood is used extensively for the production of **paper**, **pulp**, **rayon**, **matches**, and **newsprint**.
 
• **Wildlife:** The region is home to many **fur-bearing animals** that have adapted to the cold with thick coats, such as the **Sable**, **Mink**, **Ermine**, **Arctic Fox**, **Lynx**, and **Siberian Tiger**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cold Deserts Region:** This region is characterized by **extreme aridity** and **low temperatures** throughout the year. Examples include **Antarctica**, **Greenland**, and the **Gobi Desert**. In India, the **Ladakh** region is a prime example of a **Cold Desert**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cool Temperate Grassland Region:** These are vast **treeless plains** found in the interior of continents. They are known by different names such as **Steppes** (Eurasia), **Prairies** (North America), **Pampas** (South America), **Veld** (South Africa), and **Downs** (Australia). They are dominated by **nutritious grasses** rather than forests. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Equatorial Lowland Region:** Located between **0° and 10° North and South** of the equator, this region experiences **high temperature** and **heavy rainfall** (convectional) throughout the year. It is home to **Tropical Rainforests** (Selvas), characterized by high **biodiversity** and **hardwood trees**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Environmental Role:** The Taiga acts as a massive **carbon sink**, helping to regulate **global climate** by absorbing large amounts of **carbon dioxide** from the atmosphere.

questions.question: What is rural development concerned with?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Economic growth and social justice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rural development** is a comprehensive term that focuses on the action for the **social and economic upliftment** of rural areas. It is concerned with the **improvement of the quality of life** and economic well-being of people living in relatively isolated and sparsely populated areas.
 
• The core objective of rural development is **Economic growth and social justice**. It aims at increasing **productivity** and providing **equitable opportunities** to the rural population to ensure that the benefits of growth reach the poorest of the poor. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• It involves the development of **infrastructure**, such as **roads**, **electricity**, and **irrigation**, alongside social components like **literacy**, **healthcare**, and **sanitation**.
 
• **Rural development** is not concerned with the **improvement of foreign trade relations**, as that falls under the domain of **International Trade** and the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **expansion of industrial zones** generally pertains to **urban industrialization** and the manufacturing sector, rather than the multi-dimensional development of rural livelihoods. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **development of metropolitan areas** is the focus of **urban planning** and the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**, which is distinct from the challenges faced by rural communities. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Framework:** In **India**, the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act** of **1992** provided a legal basis for rural local self-government. It mandated the creation of **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** to empower people at the **village**, **intermediate**, and **district** levels to plan for **economic development** and **social justice**.
 
• **Demographic Fact:** According to the **2011 Census**, approximately **68.8%** of **India's** population lives in rural areas. This highlights the critical importance of rural development for the overall **National Income** and **GDP** growth of the **country**.
 
• **Key Government Schemes:**
 
 
• **MGNREGA (2005):** The **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act** ensures **100 days** of wage employment in a **financial year** to every household to enhance **livelihood security**.
 
• **PMGSY (2000):** The **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana** was launched to provide **all-weather road connectivity** to unconnected rural habitations.
 
• **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM):** Aimed at **poverty alleviation** through the promotion of **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**.
 
 
 
• **Dimensions of Rural Development:** It encompasses **human resource development** (literacy, especially female literacy, education, and skill development), **land reforms**, and the development of **productive resources** of each locality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Social Justice Element:** This involves the **eradication of poverty** and **reducing inequalities** in income and wealth. It also focuses on the **inclusion of marginalized sections** like **Scheduled Castes (SC)**, **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**, and **women** in the development process.
 
• **Economic Growth Element:** This refers to the sustained increase in the **agricultural output**, **rural industries**, and **services sector** within rural geographies to improve the **per capita income** of rural residents.
 
• **Sustainability:** Modern rural development emphasizes **sustainable development**, ensuring that the use of **natural resources** like **water** and **soil** does not compromise the needs of **future generations**.

questions.question: Which temple's garbhagriha houses a Chaturmukha (four-faced) Vishnu image?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshmana Temple, Khajuraho**__.

• The temple was built by the **Chandela King Yashovarman** between **930 AD** and **950 AD**. It is dedicated to **Lord Vishnu**, specifically in the form of **Vaikuntha Vishnu**.
 
• The **Garbhagriha** (sanctum sanctorum) of the temple houses a unique **Chaturmukha** or four-faced image of **Vishnu**. While the main faces visible to the devotee are the **Human** face in the center, the **Narasimha** (lion) face on one side, and the **Varaha** (boar) face on the other, it represents the complete **Vaikuntha** iconography which historically includes a fourth face (Kapila) at the back.
 
• This temple follows the **Nagara style** of architecture and is built on a **Panchayatana** plan, meaning the main shrine is surrounded by four smaller subsidiary shrines at the corners of the high platform.
 
• The temple is renowned for its intricate carvings and erotic sculptures, which are a hallmark of the **Chandela dynasty's** artistic achievements in the **10th century**.

__

• Located in the **Lalitpur district** of **Uttar Pradesh**, this temple dates back to the **Gupta Period** (around **500 AD**).
 
• It is one of the earliest known **Panchayatana** temples in **North India**.
 
• While it is dedicated to **Vishnu** and features the famous **Sheshashayi Vishnu** relief, it does not house the **Chaturmukha** idol in the main sanctum like the Lakshmana temple.
 
 
 
• **Meenakshi Temple, Madurai**:
 
 
• Located on the southern bank of the **Vaigai River** in **Tamil Nadu**, it is a masterpiece of **Dravidian architecture**.
 
• The temple is primarily dedicated to **Meenakshi** (a form of Goddess **Parvati**) and **Sundareshwarar** (a form of **Lord Shiva**).
 
• It features massive **Gopurams** (gateway towers) covered in thousands of colorful stone figures of gods and demons.
 
 
 
• **Brihadiswara Temple, Thanjavur**:
 
 
• Built by **Emperor Raja Raja Chola I** and completed in **1010 AD**, it is also known as the **Rajarajeshwaram** temple.
 
• It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and is dedicated to **Lord Shiva**.
 
• It features one of the largest **Shiva Lingas** in India and a massive monolithic **Nandi** (bull) statue.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Lakshmana Temple** is significant because it was the first of the major temples built by the **Chandelas** in their capital, **Khajuraho**.
 
• The iconography of the **Vaikuntha Vishnu** idol is highly specific; the **human face** represents **Vasudeva**, the **lion face** represents **Sankarshana** (Narasimha), and the **boar face** represents **Pradyumna** (Varaha). This reflects the **Pancharatra** philosophy of **Vaishnavism**.
 
• The **Khajuraho Group of Monuments** was designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1986** due to its unique architectural style and historical importance.
 
• Architecturally, the temple consists of an **Ardhamandapa** (entrance porch), **Mandapa** (hall), **Maha-mandapa**, and the **Vimana** (shrine tower) over the **Garbhagriha**.

questions.question: Mr. X travelled 810 km, 492 km and 988 km at a speed of 30 km/hr, 12 km/hr and 38 km/hr, respectively. Find his average speed in km/hr.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance = 810 + 492 + 988 = 2290 km

Individual Times = (810 ÷ 30) + (492 ÷ 12) + (988 ÷ 38) = 27 + 41 + 26 = 94 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 2290 ÷ 94 = 1145 ÷ 47

On dividing 1145 by 47, we get 24 as quotient and 17 as remainder.

**∴ Answer = 24 17/47**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Distance 1 (d₁) = 810 km, Speed 1 (s₁) = 30 km/hr

Distance 2 (d₂) = 492 km, Speed 2 (s₂) = 12 km/hr

Distance 3 (d₃) = 988 km, Speed 3 (s₃) = 38 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 810 km 30 km/hr 492 km 12 km/hr 988 km 38 km/hr 
 Total Journey = 2290 km 

**Calculations:**

Time taken for first part (t₁) = 810 ÷ 30 = 27 hours

⇒ Time taken for second part (t₂) = 492 ÷ 12 = 41 hours

⇒ Time taken for third part (t₃) = 988 ÷ 38 = 26 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 810 + 492 + 988 = 2290 km

⇒ Total Time = 27 + 41 + 26 = 94 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 2290 ÷ 94

⇒ Average Speed = 1145 ÷ 47 = 24 17/47 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is s₁ − s₂. When moving in opposite directions, it is s₁ + s₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a person travels for equal time intervals at speeds x and y, the average speed is the arithmetic mean (x + y) ÷ 2.

questions.question: A shopkeeper purchased 47 dozens of articles at the rate of ₹480 per dozen. He sold each one of them at the rate of ₹78. What percentage profit did he make?

Profit percentage is independent of the total quantity (47 dozens).

CP of 1 article = 480 ÷ 12 = 40

SP of 1 article = 78

Ratio CP : SP = 40 : 78 = 20 : 39

 CP = ₹40 Profit = ₹38 
 Total SP = ₹78 (CP per article = 480 ÷ 12) 

**Calculations:**

CP of 1 article = 480 ÷ 12 = ₹40

⇒ SP of 1 article = ₹78

⇒ Profit per article = 78 − 40 = ₹38

⇒ Profit % = (38 ÷ 40) × 100

Profit and Loss Percentage

Marked Price and Discount

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the effective discount is [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂ ÷ 100)]%.

Quantity Independence

The profit or loss percentage remains the same regardless of the total quantity sold, as long as the CP and SP per unit remain constant.

• Max (1500) 
 + 79 Friend Percentage = 37%

questions.question: Which type of soil is most suitable for cotton cultivation in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Black soil** is considered the most suitable for the cultivation of **cotton** in India, which is why it is often referred to as **Black Cotton Soil** or **Regur Soil**.
 
• This soil type is primarily formed from the **weathering** of **volcanic rocks** (basalt) and is largely found in the **Deccan Trap** region, covering states like **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and parts of **Karnataka** and **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• A distinctive feature of this soil is its **high moisture retention capacity**; it swells and becomes sticky when wet and develops **deep cracks** during the dry season, which aids in **self-aeration** or "self-plowing" of the soil.
 
• Chemically, Black soil is **rich in lime**, **iron**, **magnesium**, **calcium carbonate**, and **potash**, which are essential nutrients for the growth of the cotton plant, although it is generally **poor in phosphorus**, **nitrogen**, and **organic matter**.
 
• The **clayey texture** of the soil ensures that it can hold water for long periods, which is vital for cotton as it requires a steady supply of moisture during its early growth stages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• It is the **most widespread** and productive soil type in India, covering about **40%** of the total land area.
 
• Deposited by the **Indus**, **Ganga**, and **Brahmaputra** river systems, it is rich in **potash** and **phosphoric acid** but poor in nitrogen.
 
• It is highly suitable for crops like **wheat**, **paddy**, **sugarcane**, and **pulses**.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil:**
 
 
• This soil develops on **crystalline igneous rocks** in areas of **low rainfall** in the eastern and southern parts of the Deccan Plateau.
 
• The **red color** is due to a wide diffusion of **iron oxide** in crystalline and metamorphic rocks; it looks yellow when it occurs in a hydrated form.
 
• It is commonly found in **Tamil Nadu**, **Odisha**, and **Chhattisgarh** and is used for **pulses**, **millets**, and **tobacco**.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• Formed under conditions of **high temperature** and **heavy rainfall**, leading to intense **leaching** (the washing away of nutrients like silica and lime).
 
• It is **acidic** in nature and **poor in organic matter**, making it less fertile unless treated with manures and fertilizers.
 
• It is found in the **Western Ghats**, **Odisha**, and parts of the **North-east**; it is excellent for growing **cashew nuts**, **tea**, and **coffee**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cotton Cultivation Requirements:** **Cotton** is a **Kharif crop** that requires **6 to 8 months** to mature. It thrives in climates with a temperature between **21°C and 30°C**.
 
• **Climatic Conditions:** For successful harvesting, cotton needs at least **210 frost-free days** and **bright sunshine** during its growth.
 
• **Global Position:** **India** is one of the **largest producers** of cotton in the world, and the textile industry remains a backbone of the **Indian economy**.
 
• **Geographical Distribution:** The **Black soil region** of the **Deccan Plateau** is the primary cotton-producing belt, particularly the **tapti** and **narmada** river valleys.

questions.question: If x = asinθ and y = acosθ, then find the relation between x, y and a.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Square and sum both equations to eliminate the parameter θ.

Apply the fundamental identity: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

The sum x² + y² equals a²(sin²θ + cos²θ), which simplifies to a².

This result represents a circle with radius a centered at the origin.

**∴ Answer = x² + y² = a²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

x = a sinθ

y = a cosθ

**Formula used:**

Pythagorean Trigonometric Identity: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

 
 
 θ y = a cosθ (Adjacent) x = a sinθ (Opposite) Hypotenuse (a) x² + y² = a² 

**Calculations:**

From the given equations:

⇒ sinθ = x ÷ a

⇒ cosθ = y ÷ a

Squaring both equations:

⇒ sin²θ = x² ÷ a²

⇒ cos²θ = y² ÷ a²

Adding the two squared equations:

⇒ sin²θ + cos²θ = (x² ÷ a²) + (y² ÷ a²)

⇒ 1 = (x² + y²) ÷ a²

⇒ x² + y² = a²

**∴ The correct answer is (1).**

Fundamental relations in trigonometry: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.

A circle with radius r centered at origin has parametric equations x = r cosθ and y = r sinθ, yielding x² + y² = r².

Elimination of Parameter

For functions involving secθ and tanθ, use the subtraction method: (x/a)² − (y/b)² = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1.

questions.question: Folk songs of Haryana are commonly known by which of the following names?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Folk songs** of **Haryana** are primarily and popularly known as **Raganis**. These songs are an integral part of the state's cultural identity and are often performed during social gatherings, festivals, and folk theatre. ***Hence, the option Raganis is correct.***
 
• **Raganis** are deeply rooted in the **Saang** (or Swang) tradition, which is a popular **folk theatre** form in **Haryana**, **Rajasthan**, and **Uttar Pradesh**. The songs narrate stories of bravery, mythology, romance, and moral values.
 
• The most legendary figure associated with the development of **Raganis** and **Saang** is **Pandit Lakhmi Chand** (born in **1903**), who is often referred to as the **Suryakavi** (Sun Poet) of **Haryana**. His compositions are still widely sung across the state.
 
• These folk songs are traditionally accompanied by musical instruments such as the **Sarangi**, **Harmonium**, **Dholak**, **Khadtal**, and **Ghara** (earthen pot).
 
• The themes of **Haryanvi Raganis** vary from historical legends like **Raja Harishchandra** to local folklore and contemporary social issues, making them a versatile medium of oral storytelling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhand:**

 
 
• The **Bhand** refers to traditional folk entertainers or jesters found in **North India**, **Pakistan**, and **Nepal**.
 
• They are particularly famous in **Kashmir** (known as **Bhand Pather**) and **Punjab**. Their performances involve **satire**, **mimicry**, and **slapstick comedy** to entertain the public.
 
 
 
• **Bihu:**
 
 
• **Bihu** is the most important **folk dance** and **music** tradition of the state of **Assam**.
 
• It is performed during the **Rongali Bihu** festival, which marks the **Assamese New Year** in **April**. The songs are characterized by **brisk rhythms** and themes of **love** and **nature**.
 
 
 
• **Baul:**
 
 
• **Baul** is a group of mystic minstrels from **Bengal** (comprising **West Bengal** and **Bangladesh**).
 
• Their music is a unique blend of **Sufism** and **Vaishnavism**. In **2005**, the **Baul tradition** was included in the list of **Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity** by **UNESCO**.
 
 
 
• **Haryanvi Culture and Festivals:**
 
 
• Apart from **Raganis**, **Haryana** is known for its vibrant dances like **Phag** (performed during **Holi**), **Loor** (performed by women in the month of **Phalguna**), and **Ghoomar**.
 
• The **Surajkund International Crafts Mela**, held annually in **February** in **Faridabad**, is a major event that showcases the folk arts and songs of **Haryana** to a global audience.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Kartik has ₹1407 with him. He divides this amount between his two sons, Ishan and Krish, and asks them to invest their respective shares at a compound interest rate of 10% per annum, compounded annually. It is observed that Ishan’s investment amounts to the same value after 11 years as Krish’s investment does after 12 years. How much (in ₹) did Kartik give to Krish?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of shares (Ishan : Krish) = (1 + R/100)Time Diff : 1

Difference in time = 12 − 11 = 1 year

Ratio = (1 + 10/100)¹ : 1 = 1.1 : 1 = 11 : 10

Total units = 11 + 10 = 21 units → ₹1407

Krish's share (10 units) = (1407 ÷ 21) × 10 = 67 × 10 = 670

**∴ Answer = 670**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Total amount = ₹1407, Rate (R) = 10% per annum, Time for Ishan (T1) = 11 years, Time for Krish (T2) = 12 years.

**Formula used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 Ishan (I) Krish (K) 
 
 11 Years 12 Years A Total P = ₹1407 | Rate = 10% 
 

**Calculations:**

Let the shares of Ishan and Krish be I and K respectively.

I + K = 1407

As per the question: I × (1 + 10/100)¹¹ = K × (1 + 10/100)¹²

⇒ I × (1.1)¹¹ = K × (1.1)¹²

⇒ I ÷ K = (1.1)¹² ÷ (1.1)¹¹ = 1.1

⇒ I ÷ K = 11 ÷ 10

⇒ Ratio of shares I : K = 11 : 10

⇒ Krish's share = (10 ÷ 21) × 1407

⇒ Krish's share = 10 × 67 = 670

**∴ The correct answer is 670.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount A accumulated after n years is A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where P is the principal and r is the annual interest rate.

Share Distribution Logic

In CI problems where amounts are equal after different time periods, the person with the shorter time period always receives a larger share: P₁/P₂ = (1 + r/100)⁽t² − t¹⁾.

Effective Rate of Interest

For 10% rate for 2 years, the effective CI rate is r + r + (r × r)/100 = 21%.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference for 2 years is P(R/100)² and for 3 years is [P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100)].

Q. Anita, Bhavna, Charu, Deepa, and Esha, each scored different marks. Who scored the lowest marks?

(I) Bhavna scored more than Anita but less than Charu.

(II) Deepa scored more than Anita but less than Bhavna.

options.text: Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not
Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not
Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question

questions.solution:

II. Deepa scored more than Anita but less than Bhavna.

questions.question:
Two automated lab machines start a calibration cycle at the same time.

Machine A completes one cycle every **12 minutes****.**

Machine B completes one cycle every **18 minutes****.**

After how many minutes will **both machines complete a cycle together again****?**
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the time when both machines complete a cycle together again, calculate the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of their cycle times.

Cycle times are 12 minutes and 18 minutes.

Identify the larger number: 18. Multiples of 18 are 18 (not divisible by 12) and 36 (divisible by 12).

LCM(12, 18) = 36 minutes.

**∴ Answer = 36** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Time for Machine A to complete one cycle = 12 minutes

Time for Machine B to complete one cycle = 18 minutes

**Formula used:**

Time for both machines to complete together = LCM of individual cycle times

 
• Start (0 min) A (12m) A (24m) A (36m) B (18m) B (36m) 
• Together at 36 min 

**Calculations:**

Find the prime factors of each number:

⇒ 12 = 2 × 2 × 3 = 2² × 3

⇒ 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 = 2 × 3²

To find the LCM, take the highest power of each prime factor present in the numbers:

⇒ LCM(12, 18) = 2² × 3²

⇒ LCM(12, 18) = 4 × 9 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

LCM is the smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is used to find simultaneous occurrences of events with different frequencies.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

HCF (or GCD) is the largest positive integer that divides each of the numbers without leaving a remainder.

Relation between LCM and HCF

For any two positive integers a and b: LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b.

LCM Applications

Commonly used for problems involving traffic lights, bells ringing at different intervals, or runners on a circular track meeting at the starting point.

questions.question: In which year did the Union Cabinet approve the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, named as ‘Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana’?

__
 
• The Union Cabinet approved the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, titled Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY), on 1st July 2025.
 
• The scheme was initially announced in the Union Budget 2024-25 as part of the "Prime Minister’s Package for Employment and Skilling"
 
• Effective Date: The scheme came into effect on 1st August 2025.
 
• Registration Period: Benefits apply to jobs created between 1st August 2025 and 31st July 2027.
 
• Financial Outlay: It has a total budgetary outlay of ₹99,446 Crore.
 
• Job Creation Target: Aims to incentivize the creation of more than 3.5 Crore jobs over a period of two years.
 
• Implementation: It is managed by the Ministry of Labour & Employment through the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Scheme A: First-Time Employees**

 
 
• This component focuses on individuals entering the workforce for the first time in the **formal sector**.
 
• The government provides a **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** of one month’s wage, up to **₹15,000**, paid in **three installments** directly to the employee's **EPFO** account.
 
• The eligibility criteria include a monthly salary of up to **₹1,00,000**, ensuring that a broad range of graduates and diploma holders can benefit.
 
 
 
• **Scheme B: Job Creation in Manufacturing**
 
 
• This scheme specifically targets the **manufacturing sector**, which has high potential for mass employment.
 
• Incentives are provided to both the **employee** and the **employer** with respect to their **EPFO** contributions during the first **four years** of employment.
 
• It aims to encourage companies to scale up their production capacity by reducing the cost of hiring **additional manpower**.
 
 
 
• **Scheme C: Support to Employers**
 
 
• This component is **sector-agnostic** and provides direct support to employers for every additional job created.
 
• The government reimburses the employer's **EPFO contribution** up to **₹3,000** per month for **two years** for each new employee hired.
 
• This incentive is applicable for employees earning a salary up to **₹1,00,000** per month, facilitating job creation in both the **service** and **industrial** sectors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The scheme is implemented and monitored by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** through the **Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)**, ensuring transparency and direct reaching of benefits.
 
• A key feature of **PM-VBRY** is its focus on **formalization**; it requires beneficiaries to have a **Universal Account Number (UAN)** and be registered on the **e-Shram portal** or **EPFO**.
 
• The scheme aligns with the government’s broader strategy to enhance **Ease of Doing Business** by reducing the financial burden of statutory contributions on small and medium enterprises (**MSMEs**).
 
• By linking incentives directly to **employment generation**, the government aims to bridge the gap between skill development and actual job placement, fostering a more robust **industrial ecosystem** in India.

questions.question: Find the minimum value of the quadratic expression 7x² − 7x + 22.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a quadratic expression ax² + bx + c where a > 0, the minimum value is given by (4ac − b²) ÷ 4a.

Identify coefficients: a = 7, b = −7, and c = 22.

Substitute values: Min Value = [4 × 7 × 22 − (−7)²] ÷ (4 × 7).

Calculation: Min Value = [616 − 49] ÷ 28 = 567 ÷ 28.

Simplify by dividing both by 7: 567 ÷ 7 = 81 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4.

**∴ Answer = 81/4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Quadratic expression: 7x² − 7x + 22

**Formula used:**

The minimum value of f(x) = ax² + bx + c occurs at x = −b ÷ 2a.

 
 
• Vertex (1/2, 81/4) y = 7x² − 7x + 22 Min Value = 81/4 

**Calculations:**

Compare the expression with ax² + bx + c: a = 7, b = −7, c = 22.

⇒ x-coordinate of the vertex = −(−7) ÷ (2 × 7) = 7 ÷ 14 = 1/2.

⇒ Minimum value = f(1/2) = 7(1/2)² − 7(1/2) + 22.

⇒ Minimum value = 7(1/4) − 7/2 + 22 = 7/4 − 14/4 + 88/4.

⇒ Minimum value = (7 − 14 + 88) ÷ 4 = 81/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 81/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Maximum Value of a Quadratic

questions.question: Which of the following countries serves as India’s gateway to the ASEAN region by being the only ASEAN nation sharing a land boundary with India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Myanmar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Myanmar** is the only **ASEAN** (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) member country that shares a **land boundary** with **India**, making it **India’s gateway** to **Southeast Asia**.
 
• The two nations share a **land border** of approximately **1,643 km**. This boundary is shared by **four** **North-Eastern states** of **India**: **Arunachal Pradesh**, **Nagaland**, **Manipur**, and **Mizoram**.
 
• Beyond the land border, **India** and **Myanmar** also share a **maritime boundary** in the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The strategic **location** of **Myanmar** is central to **India’s** **“Act East Policy,”** which aims to promote **economic**, **strategic**, and **cultural** relations with the vast **Asia-Pacific** region.
 
• **Myanmar** acts as a **buffer** between **India** and **China** and is the only country that sits at the intersection of **India’s** **“Neighborhood First”** policy and its **“Act East”** policy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations):**

 
 
• It was **established** on **8th August 1967** in **Bangkok**, **Thailand**, with the signing of the **ASEAN Declaration** (**Bangkok Declaration**).
 
• The **10 member states** are **Brunei**, **Cambodia**, **Indonesia**, **Laos**, **Malaysia**, **Myanmar**, **Philippines**, **Singapore**, **Thailand**, and **Vietnam**.
 
• The **motto** of **ASEAN** is **“One Vision, One Identity, One Community.”** Its **Secretariat** is located in **Jakarta**, **Indonesia**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Analysis:**
 
 
• **Bangladesh:** While it shares the **longest land border** with **India** (**4,096.7 km**), it is **not** a member of **ASEAN**; it is a member of **SAARC** and **BIMSTEC**.
 
• **Nepal:** It is a **landlocked** country sharing a border with **India** but is **not** part of the **ASEAN** group.
 
• **Bhutan:** Like **Nepal**, it is a **Himalayan** neighbor and **SAARC** member but does **not** belong to **ASEAN**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Connectivity Projects:**

 
 
• **Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project:** This project connects the **Sittwe port** in **Myanmar** to the **Mizoram** state in **India**, providing an **alternate route** to the **North-East**.
 
• **India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway:** A **1,360 km** long **highway** under construction that will connect **Moreh** (India) to **Mae Sot** (Thailand) via **Myanmar**, significantly boosting **trade** and **tourism**.
 
 
 
• **Trade and Cooperation:**
 
 
• **India** is **Myanmar’s** **fourth-largest** **trading partner**. **Major exports** from **India** include **pharmaceuticals**, **machinery**, and **iron/steel**, while **imports** consist largely of **pulses**, **beans**, and **timber**.
 
• The **Free Movement Regime (FMR)** historically allowed **tribes** living along the **border** to travel **16 km** into either country without a **visa**, reflecting the **deep-rooted** **ethnic** and **cultural** ties.

questions.question: A tank is filled by three pipes, P, Q and R, with uniform flow. The first two pipes P and Q, operating simultaneously, fill the tank in the same amount of time that it takes for the tank to be filled by pipe R alone. Pipe Q fills the tank 15 hours faster than the first pipe and 12 hours slower than pipe R. What is the time required by pipe P to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the time taken by pipe R alone be x hours.

Then time for Q = x + 12 and time for P = (x + 12) + 15 = x + 27.

Since P + Q = R, use the excess time shortcut: x = √(a × b).

Here, a = 27 (excess of P) and b = 12 (excess of Q).

x = √(27 × 12) = √324 = 18 hours.

Time required by P = x + 27 = 18 + 27 = 45 hours.

**∴ Answer = 45 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

P + Q combined time = R alone time.

Pipe Q is 15 hours faster than P (Time P = Time Q + 15).

Pipe Q is 12 hours slower than R (Time Q = Time R + 12).

**Formula used:**

Total Work = LCM of all given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2x² + 39x = x² + 39x + 324

⇒ Time for pipe P = x + 27 = 18 + 27 = 45 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 45 hours, which is option (4).**

Total Capacity = Efficiency × Time. If flow rate (e.g., liters/min) is given, Capacity = Flow Rate × Time taken to fill.

questions.question: Which of the following themes guided global campaigns for World Polio Day 2025?

options.text: End Polio: Every Child, Every Vaccine, Everywhere
Immunization for All Ages across the country
Protecting Children from Diseases, all at once
Vaccines for a Healthy Child and Healthy Future

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**End Polio: Every Child, Every Vaccine, Everywhere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The theme **"End Polio: Every Child, Every Vaccine, Everywhere"** has been adopted for the **2025** global campaigns to emphasize the final push toward total eradication. This theme highlights the necessity of reaching the most remote and vulnerable children to ensure no one is left behind in the immunization process. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **World Polio Day** is observed annually on **October 24**. This date was chosen to honor the birth of **Jonas Salk**, the American medical researcher who developed the first successful **Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccine (IPV)**.
 
• The **Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI)**, which includes partners like **WHO**, **Rotary International**, **UNICEF**, and the **CDC**, uses this theme to mobilize resources and political will. The campaign focuses on the **Strategy 2022–2026**, which aims to interrupt all poliovirus transmission globally.
 
• The statement "Immunization for All Ages across the country" is a generic health slogan often associated with broader **World Immunization Week** activities but is not the specific theme for the **2025 Polio Day**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The phrase "Protecting Children from Diseases, all at once" does not align with the official branding of the **GPEI** for the year **2025**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• "Vaccines for a Healthy Child and Healthy Future" is a common advocacy phrase but lacks the specific call to action required for the **World Polio Day 2025** campaign. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Poliomyelitis:**

 
 
• Polio is a highly infectious **viral disease** that largely affects children under **5 years of age**. It invades the **nervous system** and can cause total paralysis in a matter of hours.
 
• The virus is transmitted by person-to-person spread mainly through the **fecal-oral route** or, less frequently, by a common vehicle (e.g. contaminated water or food).
 
• There is no cure for polio; it can only be prevented through **immunization**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Vaccines:**
 
 
• **Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV):** Developed by **Albert Sabin** in **1961**. It is administered orally and consists of a mixture of live, attenuated poliovirus strains.
 
• **Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV):** Developed by **Jonas Salk** and first used in **1955**. It is administered by injection and contains inactivated (killed) virus.
 
 
 
• **Global Eradication Status:**
 
 
• As of **2024-2025**, wild poliovirus type 1 (**WPV1**) remains endemic in only two countries: **Pakistan** and **Afghanistan**.
 
• The world has successfully eradicated **WPV Type 2** (certified in **2015**) and **WPV Type 3** (certified in **2019**).
 
 
 
• **India's Success Story:**
 
 
• **India** was once considered the most difficult place in the world to eradicate polio. However, the country was officially certified **Polio-free** by the **World Health Organization** on **March 27, 2014**.
 
• The last reported case of wild polio in India was in **Howrah, West Bengal**, on **January 13, 2011**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pulse Polio Programme:** This initiative was started in India in **1995** following the **World Health Assembly** resolution in **1988**. It involves vaccinating every child under the age of **five years** during **National Immunization Days (NIDs)**.
 
• **Mission Indradhanush:** Launched by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** in **December 2014**, this program aims to strengthen and re-energize the immunization coverage in the country, ensuring high coverage for children with all available vaccines, including polio.
 
• **Circulating Vaccine-Derived Poliovirus (cVDPV):** While wild polio is nearly gone, **cVDPVs** remain a challenge in areas with low immunization coverage. The **2025** campaign theme specifically targets these gaps to ensure **Every Vaccine** reaches **Every Child** to stop these outbreaks.
 
• **Financial Commitment:** Major donors like the **Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation** have committed billions of dollars toward the **GPEI** goals for **2026**, stressing that the cost of failure would be a resurgence of the disease globally.

questions.question: Which Chalukya ruler defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakesin II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pulakesin II** (reigned **610–642 AD**) was the most powerful and illustrious ruler of the **Chalukya dynasty** of **Vatapi** (modern-day **Badami** in **Karnataka**).
 
• He is famously known for defeating **Harshavardhana**, the powerful Emperor of **Kannauj**, on the banks of the **Narmada River**.
 
• The battle took place when **Harshavardhana** attempted to expand his empire into the **Deccan** region; however, **Pulakesin II** successfully guarded the passes of the **Narmada** and forced **Harsha** to retreat.
 
• The primary source for this historical event is the **Aihole Inscription** of **634 AD**, which was composed in **Sanskrit** by his court poet **Ravikirti**.
 
• Following this victory, **Pulakesin II** assumed the title of **Parameswara** (Supreme Lord) and established himself as the **Dakshinapathapathi** (Lord of the South), while **Harsha** remained the **Uttarapathanatha** (Lord of the North).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kirttivarman I**:

 
 
• He was the father of **Pulakesin II** and ruled from **566 to 597 AD**.
 
• He is often described as the "First Maker of **Vatapi**" for his role in consolidating **Chalukya** power by defeating the **Kadambas** of **Banavasi** and the **Mauryas** of **Konkan**.
 
 
 
• **Mangalesha**:
 
 
• He was the brother of **Kirttivarman I** and acted as a regent/ruler from **597 to 610 AD** because **Pulakesin II** was a minor at the time of his father's death.
 
• His reign ended when **Pulakesin II** defeated him in a civil war to claim the throne.
 
 
 
• **Vikramaditya I**:
 
 
• He was the son of **Pulakesin II** and ruled from **655 to 680 AD**.
 
• He is credited with restoring the **Chalukya** prestige after the kingdom was temporarily occupied by the **Pallavas** following the death of his father in **642 AD**.
 
 
 
• **Harshavardhana**:
 
 
• He belonged to the **Pushyabhuti** or **Vardhana dynasty** and ruled from **606 to 647 AD**.
 
• His reign and life are documented in the **Harshacharita**, a biography written by his court poet **Banabhatta**, and the travelogues of the Chinese pilgrim **Hiuen Tsang**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Date of the Battle**: While historians debate the exact year, it is widely accepted to have occurred between **618 AD** and **630 AD**.
 
• **Diplomatic Relations**: **Pulakesin II** was so influential that he reportedly exchanged ambassadors with the **Persian King Khusrau II** in **625 AD**.
 
• **Conflict with Pallavas**: Despite his victory over **Harsha**, **Pulakesin II** engaged in a long-drawn conflict with the **Pallava dynasty**. He was ultimately defeated and killed by the **Pallava** king **Narasimhavarman I** (also known as **Mamalla**) during the **Battle of Vatapi** in **642 AD**.
 
• **Hiuen Tsang's Observation**: The Chinese traveler visited the **Chalukya** kingdom in **641 AD** and praised the military discipline and the efficient administration under **Pulakesin II**, noting that the king was obeyed with fear and respect.
